NOVA (2L+ recurrent platinum-sensitive m: NOVA (2L+ recurrent platinum-sensitive maintenance): gBRCA mPFS 21.0 vs 5.5 mo; non-gBRCA HRD+ 12.9 vs 3.8 mo; non-gBRCA all 9.3 vs 3.9 mo. Individualized starting-dose rule (Berek 2018) reduces thrombocytopenia without compromising efficacy. CBC weekly first month, then monthly. Long-term MDS/AML risk warrants pre-treatment counseling.
NP30179 (Dickinson 2022, NEJM): r/r DLBC: NP30179 (Dickinson 2022, NEJM): r/r DLBCL after ≥2 prior lines (median 3; ~33% post-CAR-T) — ORR 52%, CR 39%, mDOR ~18 mo in CR cohort. FDA accelerated approval Jun 2023; EMA Jul 2023. Distinguishing features vs other CD20×CD3 bispecifics: (1) FIXED-duration 12 cycles — finite total exposure; (2) 2:1 format with bivalent CD20 binding — higher avidity, potentially deeper responses; (3) Mandatory obinutuzumab pretreatment 7 days before C1D1; (4) IV administration only (vs SC epcoritamab). Trade-offs: requires hospital/infusion-center infrastructure; obinutuzumab adds ~7 days to time-to-treatment. Lower long-term infection burden vs continuous bispecifics owing to fixed duration. Useful sequencing post-CAR-T progression in DLBCL. Bibliographic record SRC-NP30179-DICKINSON-2022 is available; clinical claim linkage requires dual clinical sign-off.

NPM1-mutated AML is a distinct WHO 2022 / ICC 2022 entity and ELN 2022 favorable-risk category in the absence of adverse co-mutations (per SRC-ELN-AML-2022, SRC-NCCN-AML-2025, SRC-ESMO-AML-2020). For fit patients, intensive induction (7+3 cytarabine/anthracycline) remains standard 1L; oral azacitidine maintenance after CR significantly prolongs OS in non-transplant patients (QUAZAR AML-001 Wei NEJM 2020 — median OS 24.7 vs 14.8 mo, HR 0.69). For unfit patients, venetoclax + azacitidine is preferred (VIALE-A DiNardo NEJM 2020 — NPM1-mutated subgroup particularly responsive, CR/CRi ~67%, mOS 14.7 mo). NPM1-mutation MRD by RT-qPCR drives post-CR intensification decisions in younger fit patients per SRC-ELN-AML-2022.

NRG1 (neuregulin-1) gene fusion in NSCLC — predominant in invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma (~7-27% of KRAS-WT IMA). NRG1 fusions produce aberrant ligand-display driving HER2-HER3 heterodimer signalling. Zenocutuzumab (MCLA-128, Bizengri) — first-in-class HER2 × HER3 bispecific IgG1 — granted FDA accelerated approval 4 Dec 2024 for advanced NSCLC and pancreatic NRG1+ post-prior systemic therapy. eNRGy phase-2 (Schram 2024; n=204): NSCLC ORR 33%, mDOR ~9 months. RNA-NGS testing critical — DNA-only panels miss fusions in 30-40% of cases. Candidate RF until pivotal trial-Source SRC-ENRGY-SCHRAM-2024 ingested.

NRG1 fusions (~0.2% NSCLC; enriched in invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma, never-smokers) drive tumor growth via HER3 activation and downstream PI3K/AKT signaling. Zenocutuzumab (MCLA-128), an anti-HER2/HER3 bispecific antibody that blocks NRG1 binding to HER3, received FDA accelerated approval (Nov 2024) for NRG1 fusion-positive locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC and pancreatic adenocarcinoma after prior systemic therapy. CRESTONE trial (Schram et al. JCO 2024): NRG1-fusion NSCLC cohort — ORR 33% (RECIST), mDOR 7.4 mo, mPFS 8.1 mo in previously treated patients; disease control rate 73%. NRG1 fusions are mutually exclusive with EGFR, ALK, ROS1, KRAS G12C in the vast majority of cases. Standard NTRK/RET/MET panel may miss NRG1 — RNA-based sequencing required.

NTHL1 germline biallelic (homozygous or: NTHL1 germline biallelic (homozygous or compound heterozygous) pathogenic variants cause NTHL1-associated polyposis (NAP) — autosomal-recessive, attenuated/oligo-polyposis with early-onset colorectal cancer plus a broad multi-tumor spectrum: breast (~60% lifetime in women), endometrial, duodenal, urothelial, brain tumors, basal-cell carcinomas, and hematologic malignancies. Tumors carry the characteristic NTHL1 mutational signature (SBS30 — C>T at NCG and NCT contexts) from defective base-excision repair. Confirmed-carrier (biallelic) surveillance protocol (per Grolleman et al. 2019 / NCCN Genetic CRC): colonoscopy q1-2y from age 25-30 with polypectomy, EGD q3-5y from age 30, breast MRI + mammography annual from age 30-35 (women), endometrial sampling + TVUS q1-2y from 35-40, urinalysis annual, skin exam annual. Heterozygous (monoallelic) NTHL1 carriers are not currently considered at materially elevated cancer risk and do not enter surveillance — only biallelic carriers qualify. ESCAT IIA.

Nanoliposomal (PEGylated) formulation of: Nanoliposomal (PEGylated) formulation of irinotecan that prolongs circulation time and enhances tumor accumulation via the enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect, increasing intra-tumoral conversion to active metabolite SN-38 (~100-1000× more potent than parent). SN-38 stabilizes the topoisomerase-I/DNA cleavable complex, producing single-strand DNA breaks that become lethal double-strand breaks during S-phase replication. SN-38 glucuronidation by UGT1A1 to inactive SN-38G is the main inactivation pathway; UGT1A1*28 homozygotes (Gilbert-syndrome variant) and *6 carriers have impaired clearance and increased risk of severe neutropenia and diarrhea — starting-dose reduction recommended. Compared with conventional irinotecan, the liposomal carrier delivers higher and more sustained intra-tumoral SN-38 exposure at lower peak plasma drug concentrations.

Naturally occurring stilbenoid polypheno: Naturally occurring stilbenoid polyphenol; activates SIRT1 (NAD+- dependent deacetylase) and modulates AMPK signaling, mTOR, NF-κB, and estrogen-receptor pathways in preclinical models. Cancer- prevention rationale (preclinical): induces cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis in tumor cell lines, inhibits inflammation, suppresses COX-2, modulates ER signaling. Animal models show reduction in chemically induced skin, mammary, colorectal, and prostate tumors. CRITICAL LIMITATION FOR CLINICAL TRANSLATION: oral bioavailability is ~1% (extensive sulfation/glucuronidation), and human plasma concentrations achieved with supplements are 10-100× lower than active concentrations in preclinical models. No clinical trial of any size has demonstrated cancer-preventive efficacy in humans.
Naturally-occurring plant alkaloid; part: Naturally-occurring plant alkaloid; partial agonist at α4β2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (same target as varenicline, of which it is the structural prototype). Produces modest dopaminergic activation (relieving craving/withdrawal) while blocking nicotine binding. Has been used as tobacco-cessation pharmacotherapy in Eastern Europe since the 1960s; comparative trials (e.g., RAUORA 2021, CASCAID) suggest efficacy comparable to varenicline at lower cost.

Niche but essential agent for documented: Niche but essential agent for documented severe penicillin allergy (anaphylaxis, SJS, DRESS) in patients requiring Gram-negative coverage — particularly in febrile neutropenia where the standard pip-tazo / cefepime / meropenem options are excluded. Standard FN regimen for severe penicillin allergy: aztreonam 2 g IV q8h + vancomycin (MRSA + Gram-positive coverage) + metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h (anaerobic coverage if intra-abdominal source). Note the ceftazidime cross-reactivity caveat (shared aminothiazolyl side chain) — confirm allergy history specifically asks about ceftazidime. For most labeled "penicillin allergy" patients without severe immediate-type reactions, modern allergy de-labeling protocols with skin testing or graded challenge can restore access to standard β-lactams; allergy consultation often warranted before defaulting to aztreonam-based regimens. Nicotine polacrilex resin releases nicot: Nicotine polacrilex resin releases nicotine slowly across the oral mucosa during intermittent chewing (chew-and-park technique). Peak plasma concentration ~20-30 min, ~1/3 to 1/2 of inhaled cigarette peak, relieving acute craving and withdrawal while avoiding the rapid arterial pulse of smoking that drives addiction. Cancer-prevention rationale: tobacco cessation is the highest- impact modifiable intervention against lung, head-and-neck, bladder, esophageal, pancreatic, cervical, kidney, AML, and other tobacco-attributable cancers (IARC Monograph 100E — Personal Habits and Indoor Combustions). NRT roughly doubles 6-month abstinence vs. placebo (Cochrane); combining a patch (long-acting baseline) with a short-acting form (gum or lozenge) PRN improves quit rates over monotherapy. USPSTF Grade A for adult tobacco-cessation pharmacotherapy.

Nitroimidazole prodrug that diffuses pas: Nitroimidazole prodrug that diffuses passively into bacteria and protozoa, where the low redox potential of anaerobic / microaerophilic organisms reduces its 5-nitro group to reactive radical intermediates (nitroso, hydroxylamine). These intermediates damage DNA via strand breakage and helix destabilization, producing bactericidal effect. Aerobic organisms cannot reduce the prodrug efficiently — hence the selective anaerobic spectrum. Active against Bacteroides fragilis group, Clostridioides spp. (including C. difficile and C. perfringens), Fusobacterium, Peptostreptococcus, Prevotella, and the protozoa Trichomonas, Giardia, Entamoeba histolytica. NO activity against aerobic bacteria. Standard add-on for anaerobic coverage in intra-abdominal, gynecologic, and dental infections, often paired with cefepime or aztreonam in febrile neutropenia with suspected intra-abdominal source. Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) / metabolic-dysfunction- associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) with advanced fibrosis (FibroScan ≥10 kPa, FIB-4 ≥2.67, or biopsy METAVIR F3-F4) is a major emerging HCC etiology, now responsible for ~15-20% of HCC cases in Western populations and rising rapidly. Cirrhotic MASLD has annual HCC incidence ~1-2% (similar to HCV/HBV cirrhotic baseline). Non-cirrhotic MASLD with advanced fibrosis can also develop HCC (~0.04-0.2%/year — not high enough for routine surveillance per AASLD but warrants closer follow-up than steatosis alone). Comorbid T2DM, obesity, and metabolic syndrome amplify risk. Modifiable: weight loss (>7% reverses NASH histology in many; >10% can regress fibrosis), glycemic control, GLP-1 agonists (semaglutide), pioglitazone (NASH benefit), resmetirom (newly approved MASH therapy 2024). ONIVYDE (liposomal irinotecan) is FDA-ap: ONIVYDE (liposomal irinotecan) is FDA-approved for two PDAC indications: (1) 1L mPDAC in combination with oxaliplatin + 5-FU + leucovorin (NALIRIFOX regimen) based on NAPOLI-3 (Wainberg, Lancet 2023; FDA approval 2024); (2) 2L mPDAC after gemcitabine-based 1L therapy in combination with 5-FU + leucovorin based on NAPOLI-1 (Wang-Gillam, Lancet 2016; FDA approval 2015). Dose is expressed in free-base equivalents per FDA label — the salt-equivalent conversion (free base × ~1.15) is found in older literature and may cause confusion; NAPOLI-3 used 50 mg/m² free base (NALIRIFOX), NAPOLI-1 used 70 mg/m² free base (2L). Liposomal formulation is NOT interchangeable with conventional irinotecan — different pharmacokinetics, different approved indications, distinct dosing. UGT1A1 testing strongly recommended before initiation; *28/*28 homozygotes need starting-dose reduction. Atropine 0.25-1 mg SC/IV for acute cholinergic syndrome (within 30 min of infusion). Loperamide schedule for late diarrhea: 4 mg at first loose stool then 2 mg q2h until 12 h diarrhea-free. ONIVYDE not registered in Ukraine — significant access barrier.

Obesity — BMI ≥30 kg/m² (per WHO definition) — OR class 2/3 obesity with BMI ≥35 / ≥40. IARC + WCRF/AICR establish obesity as an etiological factor for ≥13 cancers: post-menopausal breast cancer, endometrial, colorectal, esophageal adenocarcinoma, gastric cardia, hepatocellular carcinoma (via NAFLD/MASH), renal cell carcinoma, ovarian, pancreatic, gallbladder, multiple myeloma, meningioma, and thyroid. Population-attributable fraction varies by cancer (~30-40% for endometrial; ~5-10% for many others). Sustained weight reduction (especially ≥10% BMI) produces meaningful cancer-incidence reduction particularly for hormonally-driven tumors. Prevention-persona RedFlag.

Adenocarcinoma esofagogástrico oligometástico por OMEC-1 (Câncer esofagógásico metásico) Consenso europeu de Delfos (Kroese et al., Eur J Cancer 2023, PMID 36947929). Definido como ≤3 lesões metastáticas distantes suscetíveis de terapia local em um paciente com doença primária controlável e aptidão ECOG 0-1. Escêndios excluídos: carcinoma peritoneal, doença leptomeníngea, >3 metástases cerebrais. RenaISSANCE / AIO-FLOT5 ensaio (NCT02578368) elegibilidade mais estreita: ≤1 envolvimento incurável do sistema orgânico, sem ascite, ≤ 1 estação retroperitoneal LN — utiliza quimio FLOT ± ressecção cirúrgica (gastrectomia/esofagitectomia + metástasectomia).
Olutasidenib (Rezlidhia, Rigel Pharmaceu: Olutasidenib (Rezlidhia, Rigel Pharmaceuticals) is the second FDA-approved IDH1-mutant inhibitor (after ivosidenib / Tibsovo, Servier 2018). Both target IDH1-R132 mutations in R/R AML; key differences: (1) olutasidenib pivotal data were in R/R AML mono (Cohort R/R, n=153, ORR/CR/CRh 35%); ivosidenib has both R/R AML mono approval AND newly-diagnosed AML approval (combined with azacitidine, AGILE trial). (2) Olutasidenib has a less prominent QTc-prolongation signal than ivosidenib but a more prominent transaminitis signal. (3) Differentiation syndrome boxed warning applies to BOTH agents (class IDH-inhibitor effect — analogous to ATRA-DS in APL). (4) Cross-resistance: switching from ivosidenib → olutasidenib at progression CAN restore response in a subset (Watts Blood 2024) — suggests IDH1-R132 second-site resistance mutations may differ between agents. NCCN-AML 2025 lists olutasidenib as a category 2A option for IDH1-mut R/R AML (alongside ivosidenib). EMA has NOT approved olutasidenib (as of 2026-04-29) — in EU, ivosidenib is the IDH1-mut R/R AML standard. One of three Ashkenazi Jewish (AJ) found: One of three Ashkenazi Jewish (AJ) founder mutations (with BRCA1 c.5266dupC / 5382insC and BRCA2 c.5946delT / 6174delT). Combined carrier frequency for the three AJ founder mutations is ~1 in 40 (~2.5%) in unselected AJ population, vs ~1 in 400 (~0.25%) for any BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant in non-AJ populations. NCCN 2025 endorses population-wide AJ founder-panel testing (3-mutation panel) regardless of family history. c.68_69delAG creates a premature termination codon in exon 2, abolishing BRCT-mediated homologous-recombination repair — full BRCA1 loss-of-function phenotype. Lifetime cancer risks consistent with BRCA1 average: breast ~60-70%, ovarian ~40-45%, contralateral breast ~50% by age 70 in carriers diagnosed at age 50. Same surveillance and risk-reduction protocols as other BRCA1 pathogenic variants (annual breast MRI from age 25-30, RRSO 35-40 after childbearing). STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff.

OpenOnco is an open, auditable oncology: OpenOnco é uma base de conhecimento de apoio à decisão de oncologia aberta e auditável e demo de navegador para clínicos, laboratórios, investidores e pacientes.
OpenOnco keeps nivolumab + ipilimumab as: OpenOnco keeps nivolumab + ipilimumab as the canonical first-line IO backbone for fit metastatic melanoma patients without absolute contraindications to dual checkpoint inhibition (CheckMate-067). Single-agent pembrolizumab is the canonical default when the patient cannot tolerate the higher autoimmune risk of dual IO (KEYNOTE-006). Relatlimab + nivolumab (anti-LAG-3 + anti-PD-1) is an additional dual-checkpoint option with a different toxicity profile (RELATIVITY-047). The chapter expects the learner to weigh autoimmune history, organ function, and disease tempo against these three IO options before reaching for targeted therapy.
OpenOnco models the first-line decision: OpenOnco models the first-line decision as a standard R-CHOP track and an intensified Pola-R-CHP track. Frailty or organ dysfunction is evaluated before intensification. Higher IPI or high-risk biology can move the learner toward the intensified track if access and contraindications are addressed.

OpenOnco models the first-line decision as an aromatase inhibitor plus a CDK4/6 inhibitor (palbociclib, ribociclib, or abemaciclib) for endocrine-sensitive metastatic disease. The intensified track is inavolisib + palbociclib + fulvestrant when the patient has a PIK3CA co-alteration in the inavolisib-eligible setting and access conditions are addressed. Germline BRCA1/2 mutation pulls a parallel option (talazoparib monotherapy or olaparib post-endocrine progression) into the discussion. Visceral crisis or imminent organ failure is an explicit gate that may push the learner toward chemotherapy even in endocrine-sensitive disease.

OpenOnco models the first-line decision as docetaxel + trastuzumab + pertuzumab (THP) for HER2-amplified metastatic disease, with trastuzumab + pertuzumab maintenance continuing after taxane completion (CLEOPATRA). HR co-positive disease adds endocrine therapy to the maintenance phase rather than replacing the HER2-directed backbone. Frailty, organ dysfunction, or cardiac contraindications are evaluated against THP before any de-intensification choice, and active visceral crisis remains a separate emergency pathway.

OpenOnco splits the first-line mCRPC dec: OpenOnco splits the first-line mCRPC decision by prior ARPI exposure. ARPI-naive mCRPC routes to abiraterone or enzalutamide; ARPI-resistant disease pulls PARP-inhibitor reasoning into the canonical first option when a BRCA1/2 mutation (or, depending on the indication, a broader HRR alteration) is present. Patients without an actionable HRR alteration who have already received an ARPI move toward docetaxel chemotherapy at the next decision point. The transition from mHSPC to mCRPC is the moment when a fresh HRR result changes the algorithm — older germline-only tests should be repeated with tumor sequencing if the original result was negative.

Orally bioavailable PI3Kα inhibitor that: Orally bioavailable PI3Kα inhibitor that selectively binds and promotes degradation of mutant p110α (PIK3CA-mut) over wild-type — improved tumor selectivity vs alpelisib. Orally bioavailable small-molecule inhib: Orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of mutant isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (mIDH1) — selective for the neomorphic R132 hotspot variants (R132H, R132C, R132G, R132L, R132S). Bimodal age distribution: adolescent growth-spurt peak (10–20y; long-bone metaphyses) and elderly secondary peak (>60y; predominantly Paget disease-associated or post-radiation). Standard-of-care multi-modal treatment (full Indications pending): neoadjuvant chemotherapy → en-bloc surgical resection (limb-salvage preferred; amputation reserved for unresectable / vascular-bundle invasion) → adjuvant chemotherapy. MAP regimen (high-dose methotrexate, doxorubicin, cisplatin) is the global standard from EURAMOS-1 (good-responder arm). Histological necrosis ≥90% at resection predicts favorable outcome; poor responders (<90% necrosis) do NOT benefit from intensification per EURAMOS-1. Ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor in any: Ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor in any child / adolescent / young adult should trigger DICER1 germline testing — the proportion of DICER1-positive cases is high (~30-60%, higher in younger and poorly-differentiated cases). Diagnosis in a postmenopausal woman has a lower (though non-zero) DICER1-positive yield. Treatment: fertility-sparing unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (USO) with staging for stage IA well-differentiated tumors in young women; total hysterectomy + bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (TAH-BSO) for postmenopausal patients or high-grade / advanced-stage disease. Adjuvant chemotherapy (BEP — bleomycin, etoposide, cisplatin — similar to germ-cell tumour regimens) for stage IC and above, or poorly-differentiated / retiform variants. Androgen excess resolves dramatically post-surgery (virilization symptoms regress but voice deepening may be permanent). Lifelong DICER1-syndrome surveillance for germline-positive survivors: contralateral ovary US q6-12 months (synchronous and metachronous DICER1-driven SLCTs reported), chest imaging (PPB risk in survivors' offspring + own residual risk), thyroid US, and abdominal-pelvic US.

PDGFRA D842V substitution mutation in advanced or metastatic GIST. The PDGFRA D842V variant accounts for approximately 6-7% of all GIST and is the most common PDGFRA exon 18 mutation (~65-70% of PDGFRA-mutant GIST). D842V confers primary resistance to imatinib, sunitinib, and regorafenib due to steric interference with drug binding at the activation loop. The type I kinase inhibitor avapritinib binds the active conformation of PDGFRA D842V and achieves ORR ~88% (NAVIGATOR phase 1; Heinrich CANCER DISCOV 2020) and confirmed ORR ~91% in the phase 3 NAVIGATOR expansion cohort. Imatinib is ineffective (historical ORR <10% for D842V) and must not be used as 1L for confirmed D842V-mutant GIST. Fires to route ALGO-GIST-1L step 1 to avapritinib (IND-GIST-1L- AVAPRITINIB-PDGFRA-D842V) instead of imatinib (IND-GIST-1L-IMATINIB). PDGFRA D842V substitution mutation in advanced or metastatic GIST. The PDGFRA D842V variant accounts for approximately 6-7% of all GIST and is the most common PDGFRA exon 18 mutation (~65-70% of PDGFRA-mutant GIST). D842V confers primary resistance to imatinib, sunitinib, and regorafenib due to steric interference with drug binding at the activation loop. The type I kinase inhibitor avapritinib binds the active conformation of PDGFRA D842V and achieves ORR ~88% (NAVIGATOR phase 1; Heinrich CANCER DISCOV 2020) and confirmed ORR ~91% in the phase 3 NAVIGATOR expansion cohort. Imatinib is ineffective (historical ORR <10% for D842V) and must not be used as 1L for confirmed D842V-mutant GIST. Fires to route ALGO-GIST-1L step 1 to avapritinib (IND-GIST-1L- AVAPRITINIB-PDGFRA-D842V) instead of imatinib (IND-GIST-1L-IMATINIB). NCCN GIST 2025 Category 1 preferred: avapritinib 300 mg PO QD for PDGFRA D842V-mutant unresectable/metastatic GIST. Detection: PDGFRA D842V is detectable on targeted NGS, hotspot PCR, or PDGFRA-specific IHC (D842V antibody). Tissue or ctDNA-based molecular testing of all GIST at diagnosis is standard of care per NCCN GIST 2025. PDGFRA non-D842V exon 18 mutations (e.g., D842del, DI842-843IM): intermediate imatinib sensitivity — these are NOT covered by this RF. The RF fires exclusively on the D842V substitution. Non-D842V exon 18 PDGFRA mutations route to imatinib (ALGO-GIST-1L step 2 default path).

Liga os receptores GH e bloqueia a dimerização dos receptores induzidas por GH, assim como a transdução do sinal a jusante, diminuindo a produção de IGF-1 sem reduzir os níveis de GH circulante — não reduz diretamente o adenoma de somatotrófos. PERSEUS maintenance arm (Sonneveld NEJM: PERSEUS maintenance arm (Sonneveld NEJM 2024, PMID 38084760): after D-VRd × 4 induction + ASCT + D-VRd × 2 consolidation, patients received daratumumab SC q4w (first 6 cycles then q8w) + lenalidomide 10 mg d1-21 until progression. Median maintenance duration ~38 months. Distinct from: (1) REG-LENALIDOMIDE-MAINTENANCE (len-only, no daratumumab — CALGB 100104 / IFM 2005-02 schema); (2) MRD-guided approaches (investigational). Key PERSEUS maintenance outcomes: 48-month PFS 84.3% (D-VRd arm) vs 67.7% (VRd arm); MRD-negativity (10⁻⁵) at 12 months post-consolidation 75.2% vs 47.5%. The PFS benefit was consistent across transplant-eligible subgroups including high-risk cytogenetics (del17p, t[4;14], t[14;16]). Daratumumab dosing transition in PERSEUS: q4w during consolidation and first 6 maintenance cycles → q8w thereafter. Some Ukrainian centers may default to q4w throughout for simplicity; both schedules are documented. POLD1 germline pathogenic variants in th: POLD1 germline pathogenic variants in the exonuclease (proofreading) domain cause PPAP — similar to POLE-PPAP but with a stronger endometrial-cancer signal in women (lifetime endometrial risk ~50% per published cohorts). Phenotype includes attenuated polyposis with early-onset CRC, endometrial cancer, and CNS tumors in some families. Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (Lynch-like): colonoscopy q1-2y starting age 20-25, endometrial sampling + TVUS q1-2y from age 30-35 in women (consider earlier given higher endometrial risk than POLE), EGD q3y from age 30, urinalysis q1y from age 30. Tumor ultramutator phenotype (TMB high) suggests immunotherapy responsiveness in advanced disease; pembrolizumab FDA- approved for TMB-H solid tumors. Risk-reducing hysterectomy + BSO after childbearing is reasonable to discuss in POLD1 carriers (analogous to Lynch INTENSIFIED-track decision). ESCAT IIA.

POLE germline pathogenic variants in the exonuclease (proofreading) domain cause polymerase proofreading–associated polyposis (PPAP) — characterized by attenuated/oligo-polyposis (typically <100 adenomas), early-onset colorectal cancer, elevated endometrial cancer risk in women, and characteristic ultramutator tumor phenotype (TMB >100 mut/Mb) with potential immunotherapy responsiveness. Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (Lynch-like; per NCCN Genetic/Familial CRC 2025): colonoscopy q1-2y starting age 20-25, EGD q3y from age 30, endometrial sampling + TVUS q1-2y from age 30-35 in women, urinalysis annual from 30 (overlap with Lynch organ spectrum). The ultramutator phenotype in POLE-mutant tumors predicts immunotherapy benefit (high TMB) — pembrolizumab is FDA- approved for TMB-high (≥10 mut/Mb) advanced solid tumors regardless of tissue; POLE-mutant CRC and endometrial benefit appears substantial in small series. ESCAT IIA (predisposition + tumor-phenotype actionability).

Two key modifications vs full FOLFIRINOX (REG-FOLFIRINOX): irinotecan 150 mg/m² (not 180) and 5-FU bolus OMITTED. Parafollicular C-cell origin — secretes: Parafollicular C-cell origin — secretes calcitonin (diagnostic + monitoring biomarker) and CEA (parallel monitoring). RAI is NOT effective (C-cells do not concentrate iodide). Germline RET testing is mandatory at diagnosis — drives: - Prophylactic thyroidectomy timing in kindred (MEN2B: <1 yr; MEN2A C634: <5 yr per ATA risk classification). - Pheochromocytoma screening (plasma metanephrines / urinary catechols annually) — RET drives both MTC and adrenal medullary tumors. - Hyperparathyroidism screening in MEN2A. Therapy: - Localized: total thyroidectomy + central compartment LN dissection. - Advanced / unresectable (calcitonin doubling time <1 yr or structural progression): selpercatinib (LIBRETTO-001 / -531) or pralsetinib (ARROW) for RET-mutant MTC — superior to multikinase TKIs (vandetanib ZETA / cabozantinib EXAM remain alternatives, significant toxicity). - RET-WT (RAS-mutant or other): no targeted option; cabozantinib / vandetanib by default. Calcitonin doubling time <6 months portends very poor survival; <2 yr drives systemic-therapy decisions even without RECIST progression.

Pediatric cystic nephroma is a strong DI: Pediatric cystic nephroma is a strong DICER1-syndrome signal — diagnosis in any child should trigger DICER1 germline testing AND cascade-testing of parents + siblings. Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome is a separate (non- DICER1) etiology that shares the Wilms-spectrum abdominal-tumour surveillance protocol (abdominal US q3-4 months from birth to age 7; AFP q2-3 months from birth to age 4 — focused on hepatoblastoma). Treatment: maximal safe surgical resection (nephron-sparing partial nephrectomy when anatomically feasible; total nephrectomy if not). Histopathology after resection is critical — distinguishes pure cystic nephroma (benign-borderline, surveillance only) from cystic partially differentiated nephroblastoma (Wilms-spectrum, requires adjuvant chemo per stage) and from progression to anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney (high-grade malignant, requires multimodal therapy). Lifelong DICER1-syndrome surveillance for germline-positive survivors: chest imaging (PPB risk), abdominal-pelvic US (ovarian, Sertoli-Leydig risk in girls), thyroid US, and CNS imaging (pineoblastoma, pituitary blastoma risk under age 5).
Pediatric infection screening is broader: Pediatric infection screening is broader than adult — include CMV / herpes given immunosuppression on VAC and likelihood of reactivation in neonates / infants. HBsAg+ infants: confirm vertical transmission, consult pediatric hepatology, entecavir / tenofovir prophylaxis adapted to weight. HIV+ pediatric: ART coordination critical — TRK inhibitors (larotrectinib, entrectinib) are CYP3A4 substrates, avoid CYP3A4 inhibitors. Pneumocystis prophylaxis (TMP-SMX) is standard on cytotoxic arm. Surfaces hold via parallel pre-treatment workup.
Pediatric-inspired adolescent-young-adul: Pediatric-inspired adolescent-young-adult protocols dominate in fit <40; >65 mortality from induction toxicity is high. Mini-HCVD + inotuzumab/blinatumomab achieves better tolerability with comparable CR rates.

Pexidartinib (PLX3397), um inibidor do CSF1R/KIT/FLT3, é aprovado pela FDA (agosto de 2019) para doentes adultos com tumor de células gigantes sintomáticas tenossinoviais (TCG) associado a morbidade grave ou limitações funcionais não susceptíveis de melhorar com a cirurgia. Ensaio de fase III ILLUMINATO (Tap et al., Lancet 2019): N=120 (pexidarinib vs placebo, crossover design); endpoint primário ORR na semana 25 pelo RECIST 1,1 e TTP-MRI. ORR: 38% (RECIST) vs 0% placebo (p<0,0001); 56% por TTP -MRI vs0%. MDOR: não atingido na mediana de 23,1 meses de seguimento. Taxa de benefício clínico: 56%. Segurança: hepatotoxicidade significativa (hepatite colestática, incluindo um caso fatal em extensão aberta); elevações ALT/AST em ~51%; programa REMS da FDA obrigatório. EMA aprovado para a mesma indicação (2020). Não é necessário diagnóstico de acompanhante de biomarcadores — todos os doentes TGCT são elegíveis com base em critérios clínicos (sintomáticos, resistentes à cirurgia). Não é necessário o teste de fusão CSF1R IHC ou COL6A3-CSF1 para o início do tratamento.

Pheochromocytoma is a catecholamine-secr: Pheochromocytoma is a catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumor of adrenal medullary origin; extra-adrenal counterparts (paragangliomas) arise from sympathetic / parasympathetic ganglia (head/neck, thoracic, abdominal). They are biologically and clinically a single spectrum (PPGL); this entity is anchored to the adrenal subset for ICD-10 cleanliness but cross-references SDHx-driven extra-adrenal paragangliomas in prevention workstream notes. Hereditary fraction is the highest known among adult cancers (~30–40%). NCCN and Endocrine Society recommend germline panel testing (RET, VHL, SDHB/C/D/AF2, NF1, TMEM127, MAX, FH) for ALL patients with PPGL — not restricted by family history. This makes PPGL a sentinel disease for hereditary cancer surveillance pathways (RET → MEN2 prophylactic thyroidectomy; VHL → multi-organ surveillance; SDHB → lifetime PPGL + RCC surveillance). Classical clinical triad: headache + palpitations + sweating; many patients present with paroxysmal or sustained hypertension. Pineoblastoma is one of the canonical em: Pineoblastoma is one of the canonical embryonal CNS manifestations of DICER1 syndrome — diagnosis in any child should trigger DICER1 germline testing regardless of family history. Distinct from pineocytoma (Grade 1, benign) and pineal parenchymal tumour of intermediate differentiation (PPTID, Grade 2-3). Treatment philosophy parallels other embryonal CNS tumours: maximal safe surgical resection (gross total resection is prognostically dominant); craniospinal irradiation in age-appropriate patients (deferred under age 3 due to neurocognitive toll); adjuvant high-dose chemotherapy regimens (often COG/SIOP protocols with carboplatin, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, cisplatin, etoposide combinations + autologous stem-cell rescue in high-risk cases). Trilateral retinoblastoma (bilateral RB1-carrier with pineal pineoblastoma) historically had near-uniform mortality; modern MRI surveillance from RB1-carrier diagnosis has shifted some cases to earlier detection with improved outcomes.

Pituitary blastoma is the strongest sing: Pituitary blastoma is the strongest single-tumour DICER1-syndrome signal — diagnosis in any infant should immediately trigger DICER1 germline testing AND cascade-testing of parents (>95% pituitary blastomas carry pathogenic germline DICER1). Distinct from far-more- common pituitary adenomas (which are not DICER1-driven and are typically adult-onset). Treatment: trans-sphenoidal or trans-cranial resection (technically challenging in infants — pituitary blastomas are bleeding-prone and locally invasive); adjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-VP16-cyclophosphamide-based regimens reported in case series); RT generally avoided under age 3 due to severe neurocognitive + endocrine toll. Hypercortisolism management (medical adrenal blockade, sometimes adrenalectomy) is an essential pre-operative bridge. Lifelong endocrine replacement (hydrocortisone, growth hormone, thyroid, gonadal axis) after curative-intent resection. Lifelong DICER1-syndrome surveillance for survivors.

Pleuropulmonary blastoma is the canonica: Pleuropulmonary blastoma is the canonical DICER1-syndrome cancer — PPB diagnosis in any child should trigger DICER1 germline testing AND cascade-testing of parents + siblings. The Type I → Type II → Type III progression model is unique among pediatric cancers in offering a true surveillance-curable precursor lesion (Type I PPB is histologically benign-appearing cystic disease that, if completely resected, has excellent prognosis; if left in situ, may progress to the higher-mortality Type II/III). Treatment by type: Type I — complete surgical resection; close follow-up imaging for new cysts or solid transformation. Type II/III — surgical resection (often combined lobectomy / pneumonectomy with CNS prophylaxis consideration); IVADo (ifosfamide, vincristine, actinomycin-D, doxorubicin) or similar sarcoma-style regimens; CNS-directed therapy for Type III given high CNS-relapse risk. Distinguishing PPB Type I from congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM) — the most common pediatric cystic lung lesion — is the major early-life diagnostic challenge: family history of DICER1-related malignancies + multi-locular or septated cysts argue for PPB over CPAM and should prompt referral to...

Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) with persistent anovulation and resulting chronic unopposed estrogen exposure on endometrial epithelium — endometrial cancer RR ~2.7 (Haoula et al. Hum Reprod Update 2012); earlier age of onset (40s vs typical 60s) common. Often accompanied by obesity + insulin resistance + type-2 diabetes — additional independent endometrial-cancer risk factors that compound risk multiplicatively. Endometrioid (type I) histology predominates. Frequently underrecognized in women relying on hormonal contraception that masks anovulation. Risk modifiable: combined hormonal contraception (estrogen + progestin) OR cyclic progestin OR levonorgestrel IUD restore endometrial protection. Weight loss + metformin (in T2DM/IR PCOS) provide additional risk reduction. Prevention-persona RedFlag (§20 v0.3 reproductive expansion).

Polyene macrolide that binds ergosterol: Macrólido polieno que liga o ergosterol à membrana celular fúngica, formando canais transmembranos que interrompem a integridade da membrana, permitem vazamento de conteúdo intracelular (potássio, magnésio) e produzem atividade fungicida. A encapsulação lipossómica em vesículas unilamelares (~80 nm) fornece preferencialmente anfotericina para células fúngicas através da afinidade do ergosterol, poupando simultaneamente as membranas celulares de mamíferos (que contêm colesterol com menor afinidade de anfotericina), reduzindo significativamente a nefrotoxicidade, as reações à perfusão e o desperdício de eletrólitos versus o desoxicolato de anphoterisina B convencional. Polyfunctional alkylating agent: each of: Polyfunctional alkylating agent: each of three ethyleneimine groups generates an aziridinium intermediate that alkylates DNA primarily at N7 of guanine, producing intra-strand and inter-strand cross-links → DNA replication arrest and apoptosis. Active metabolite TEPA (triethylenephosphoramide, formed by hepatic CYP3A4 / CYP2B6 desulfuration) contributes equally to cytotoxicity. Highly lipid-soluble — penetrates CNS readily (CSF levels ~100% of plasma), the basis of its central role in PCNSL induction (MATRix), CNS-relapse-risk lymphoma conditioning (TBC = thiotepa + busulfan + cyclophosphamide; TT-BCNU), and intrathecal use for leptomeningeal disease.

Potent ATP-competitive small-molecule in: Potent ATP-competitive small-molecule inhibitor of all three AKT serine/threonine kinase isoforms (AKT1, AKT2, AKT3) within the PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling pathway. Suppresses downstream phosphorylation of effector substrates (FOXO, GSK3, TSC2, MDM2, 4EBP1 via mTORC1), reducing proliferation and survival signaling and partially reversing endocrine-therapy resistance in HR+ breast cancer driven by PI3K-pathway alterations. Tumors with activating PIK3CA / AKT1 mutations or PTEN loss (~40-50% of HR+/ HER2- mBC after CDK4/6i) are enriched for response. Pivotal evidence CAPItello-291 (HR+/HER2- mBC after AI ± CDK4/6i): capivasertib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant — overall mPFS 7.2 vs 3.6 mo HR 0.60; in PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered subgroup mPFS 7.3 vs 3.1 mo HR 0.50. FDA approval Nov 2023 (mutation-restricted).
Potent inhibitor of multiple receptor ty: Potent inhibitor of multiple receptor tyrosine kinases: VEGFR-1/2/3, PDGFR-α/β, c-KIT, FLT3, CSF-1R, RET. Antiangiogenic + direct antiproliferative effects. In pNET: anti-VEGF/PDGF pathway disrupts tumour neovasculature; direct TKI effect on pNET cells that overexpress VEGFR. Raymond 2011 NEJM: mPFS 11.4 vs 5.5 mo (HR 0.42) in well- differentiated progressive pNET.

Pre-existing autoimmune disease is prese: Pre-existing autoimmune disease is present in ~10-15% of patients eligible for ICI therapy; historically excluded from pivotal trials. Real-world data (Abdel-Wahab 2018, 3557 pts) shows 55% experienced irAE flare and ~29% required systemic immunosuppression beyond steroids. Risk stratification by SITC 2021: - **Low risk** (generally safe to proceed with monitoring): thyroiditis, vitiligo, stable psoriasis, type 1 diabetes — irAE flare mild, manageable. - **Moderate risk** (proceed with specialist input): RA, IBD (Crohn/UC), sarcoidosis, sicca syndrome, psoriatic arthritis — flare rate ~50%; baseline DMARDs often OK to continue (methotrexate, HCQ but NOT high-dose steroids or anti-TNF at start). - **High risk** (strongest caution; consider alternative if available): active autoimmune hepatitis, myasthenia gravis, inflammatory myopathy, neuromyelitis optica — flare can be life-threatening; benefit-risk discussion mandatory. Pulmonary sarcoidosis specifically: ICI-induced sarcoid-like reactions are well-documented (5-7% of patients on ICI), often mimicking disease progression on imaging. Preferred 5-HT3 antagonist for HEC and f: Preferred 5-HT3 antagonist for HEC and for multi-day chemotherapy regimens because of long half-life and demonstrated superiority in delayed-phase CINV control vs ondansetron in head-to-head trials (Saito 2009, Aapro 2014). Triple antiemetic regimen for HEC: NK1 antagonist (aprepitant or fosaprepitant) + palonosetron 0.25 mg IV + dexamethasone 12 mg IV day 1, with dex tapered through delayed phase. Akynzeo (netupitant 300 mg + palonosetron 0.5 mg) fixed-dose oral capsule simplifies triple therapy to two pills (Akynzeo + dex) on day 1. Lowest QT signal in 5-HT3 class — preferred when ondansetron contraindicated due to QT concerns or cardiac comorbidity. Minimal CYP-mediated metabolism makes it the safer 5-HT3 choice in polypharmacy patients (e.g., patients on CYP3A4 inhibitors).
Preferred BTKi for CLL 1L per NCCN 2025: Preferred BTKi for CLL 1L per NCCN 2025 (over ibrutinib due to less cardiac toxicity). ELEVATE-TN (1L CLL): superior PFS vs Clb+O at 5y; ELEVATE-RR (r/r): non-inferior to ibrutinib with better safety. Funding pathway must be confirmed pre-start in Ukraine.
Preferred BTKi over ibrutinib in modern: Preferido BTKi sobre ibrutinib em modernas diretrizes CLL/MCL (ELEVATE-RR para r/r CLL — eficácia comparável, menos eventos cardíacos/hipertensão). ELEVate-TN: 1L dados CLL também favoráveis. Ucrânia: registrado, mas NÃO reembolsado via NSZU — financiamento...

Prevention-persona RedFlag (CHARTER §3 a: Prevention-persona RedFlag (CHARTER §3 amended 2026-05-18 Path A, HCP-mediated). Fires when patient profile shows chronic H. pylori (positive UBT / stool antigen / biopsy histology / stool PCR) AND no confirmed gastric malignancy. Engine routes such patients to a PreventionPlan recommending eradication therapy (per IND-H-PYLORI-PREVENTION-ERADICATION) as the etiological-cancer- prevention pathway. Evidence for H. pylori → gastric cancer causation (IARC Group 1): multiple Cochrane meta-analyses show eradication reduces gastric adenocarcinoma incidence (RR ~0.54-0.66, NNT ~15-50 depending on population baseline incidence). Effect is stronger in high-incidence populations and in younger individuals where atrophic gastritis / intestinal metaplasia has not yet developed. Evidence for H. pylori → gastric MALT lymphoma: eradication is the first-line treatment for early-stage gastric MALT lymphoma, with Wotherspoon regression in ~70-80% of cases (especially t(11;18)- negative). This is treatment-persona territory (existing MALT lymphoma in setting of confirmed H. pylori → treatment Indication, not yet authored) — distinct from prevention persona (chronic H. pylori → prevent MALT/adenocarc...

Prevention-persona RedFlag (CHARTER §3 amended 2026-05-18 Path A, HCP-mediated). Fires when patient profile shows chronic HCV (HCV-RNA detectable OR HCV-Ab+ with persistent viremia >6 months) AND no confirmed B-cell NHL diagnosis. Engine routes such patients to a PreventionPlan recommending DAA antiviral therapy (per IND-CHRONIC-HCV-PREVENTION-DAA) as the etiological-cancer-prevention pathway. Evidence for HCV → NHL causation (IARC Group 1): multiple cohort studies show 2-3x increased risk of indolent B-cell NHL in chronic HCV carriers; epidemiology especially robust for MZL subtypes. DAA cure (SVR12) has been associated with reduced NHL incidence in post-treatment cohorts (de-Re et al. and others) and with regression of established HCV-associated indolent NHL (the basis of IND-HCV-MZL-1L-ANTIVIRAL for the treatment persona). This is a STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode exemption (sources cited, draft flag set). Engine consumption is DEFERRED to v0.2 implementation wave — the PreventionPlan code path does not yet exist; this RF lands as schema-valid declarative content awaiting that wave.
Prevention-persona RedFlag combining red: Prevention-persona RedFlag combining red-meat ≥500g/week + processed-meat ≥50g/day thresholds per WCRF/AICR + IARC Monograph 114. Severity:major because processed-meat exposure is Group-1 carcinogen with population-attributable fraction ~13% for CRC (WCRF/AICR). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending dietary substitution + CRC screening per USPSTF. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode. Coexists with existing RF-LIFESTYLE-PROCESSED-MEAT-PREVENTION — both may fire.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for ATM heter: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para portadores heterozigotos ATM. Distinção do fenótipo A-T biallélico é crítica: heterozygotos têm predisposição ao câncer apenas (sem fenónimo neurológico). Rotas motoras para vigilância mamaria reforçada + vigilância pancreática para portadoras FDR-of- PDAC por consórcio CAPS 2022; consciência da próstata para homens. STUB pendente de sinalização de duas Co-Lead por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for BAP1 synd: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para história familiar da síndrome BAP1. STUB pendente de assinatura de duas Co-Lead.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for BARD1 het: Prevention-persona RedFlag for BARD1 heterozygous carriers. Engine routes to enhanced breast surveillance + ovarian symptom-driven workup. NCCN places BARD1 in moderate-elevated breast tier (annual mammography from age 40; consider MRI). Triple-negative subset signal may justify earlier or MRI-inclusive screening in family- history-stratified cohorts. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for BHD/FLCN: Prevention-persona RedFlag for BHD/FLCN confirmed carriers. Multi- organ surveillance: abdominal MRI q2-3y from age 20 for RCC (avoid radiation; many BHD lesions are hybrid oncocytic + slow-growing); chest HRCT baseline + symptom-driven (spontaneous pneumothorax triggers high-resolution imaging); dermatology q1y for skin surveillance. Nephron-sparing surgery (partial nephrectomy) preferred for ≤3cm renal lesions given multifocal/bilateral disease pattern. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for BRIP1 het: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para portadores heterozigotos BRIP1. NCCN avalia RRSO na idade de envelhecimento completa ou 45-50 anos; não recomendam rastreamento do câncer ovário da população. Vigilância da mama por esquemas populacionais gerais a menos que história familiar eleve o risco independentemente. STUB pendente dois-Co-Lead sinal por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for C. sinens: Prevention-persona RedFlag for C. sinensis-driven cholangiocarcinoma prevention. Fires on any documented exposure history with confirmatory testing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending praziquantel (if active infection) + lifelong hepatobiliary surveillance (US + CA 19-9 q12mo from age 40 in heavily-exposed cohorts). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA. East-Asian endemic belt has 10-50x higher cholangiocarcinoma incidence than non-endemic Western populations. Geographic context: relevant for East-Asian diaspora, immigrants, refugees, adoptees. Companion to RF-OPISTHORCHIS-CHOLANGIO-PREVENTION (Mekong-region liver-fluke pathway, biologically similar mechanism — identical surveillance protocol).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CDH1 / HD: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para portadores confirmados CDH1 / HDGC por IGCLC 2020 internacional diretriz. Gastrectomia total profilática (PTG) recomendado 20-30 anos (intervalo 18-40 por discussão individualizada); vigilância endoscópica é reconhecido inferior ao PTG (focos de anel de células de aro difuso pouco visíveis) mas oferecido a portadores de declínio de PTG. Portadores femininos: vigilância de mama BRCA-estilo a partir de 30 anos. STUB pendente de sinalização de duas-Co-Lead por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CDKN2A-sp: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para portadores específicos de CDKN2A (RF geno-específico versus o FAMMM RF mais amplo). Vigilância pancreática por CAPS Consortium 2018/2020: alternando EUS + RM/MRCP abdominal a cada 12 meses a partir da idade 40 OR 10 anos antes da primeira PDAC em família (se for o caso anterior). Vigilia do melanoma: exame anual da pele do corpo inteiro + dermoscopia a partir de 10-12 anos; mapeamento de fotografia para múltiplos moles atípicos. Paciente deve conhecer proteção solar agressiva + coorte CDKNI2A-especifico ao longo da vida. STUB pendente de dois-Co-Lead sinal por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CHEK2 het: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para portadores heterozigotos CHEK2. Estimativas de risco variam substancialmente de acordo com a variante: truncar > erva > erro. Rotas motoras para a vigilância mamária aprimorada (mamografia anual a partir da idade 40 + consideração de RM), rastreamento de CRC modestamente apertado (colonoscopia a partir de 40 anos com intervalo q5y por NCCN), e consciência da próstata a partir dos 40-45 anos para os homens com c. 1100delC. STUB pendente de sinalização de duas-Co-Lead por CHARTER § 6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CMMRD con: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para CMMRD confirmada coorte pediátrica portadora. Vigilância por Cuidado para CmmRD (C4CMMRD) consórcio 2014: RM de corpo inteiro anualmente a partir do diagnóstico; RM do cérebro q6mo a partir da idade 2; colonoscopia q6MO a partir de 6 anos; endoscopia GI superior + cápsula de pequenas bolhas a partir dos 8 anos; CBC + eletroforese proteica sérico + abdominal US q6Mo. Teste de cascata de irmãos + confirmação do portador de MMR parental. Imunoterapia (anti-PD-1) eficaz em cânceres relacionados com a DRCMM estabelecidos (Bouffet 2016, série Larkin/CheckMate). STUB pendente de sinalização de duas Co-Lead por CHARTER §6.1 modo dev.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for Cronkhite: Prevention-persona RedFlag for Cronkhite-Canada syndrome. risk_category set to chronic_condition (not genetic) because etiology is acquired autoimmune-like + non-Mendelian. Surveillance: colonoscopy q1-2y from diagnosis; upper endoscopy q1-2y; small-bowel capsule q2y; treat active disease with immunosuppression (prednisone taper + azathioprine maintenance) + nutritional support (protein replacement, electrolyte correction). Mortality reduced markedly with immuno- suppression treatment. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for DES in-ut: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para a coorte de exposição in-utero do DES. O controle é intensificado em relação à população geral (pélvico anual com cuidadosa inspeção vaginal/cervical; colposcopia se citologia anormal; mamografia no limiar de idade mais jovem por risco de modificador NCCN; considerar o rastreamento mamario RM adjuvante com risco duplicado). STUB pendente a dois-Co-Lead sinal por CHARTER §6.1 dev-modo.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for DICER1 co: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para coorte confirmada de portadores DICER1. Vigilância pediátrica por Registro Internacional de PPB / Recomendações IDSDB: - TC de tórax q4-6 mo do nascimento até 3 anos de idade q6-12 mo até 8 anos de vida. - US abdominal q3-6 mo de nascimento até 8 filhos. - basal de UTI da tireóide por 8 anos + q3-5 anos. - USA pélvica em portadoras do sexo feminino de menarquia. - base de RM do cérebro + motivado por sintomas. Ooforectomia de redução de risco não foi endossada para prevenção de Sertoli-Leydig. STUB pendente dois-Co-Lead sinal por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for EBV-drive: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para prevenção do câncer por EBV em hospedeiros imunocomprometidos. Ao contrário do VHC/HBV/H. pylori, não existe um regime anti-EBV curativo; a via de prevenção é (a) reduzir a imunossupressão quando possível, (b) o rituximab preventivo em doentes pós-transplante com aumento do DNA-EB (por diretrizes internacionais de PTLD), (c) monitorização periódica do ADN-EBB. STUB pendente Co-Lead revisão. A gating por contexto imunocompromiso adicional é deliberada — a seroprevalência do EBV é >90% em adultos imunocompetentes globalmente, por isso um RF desencadeado em EB V por si só dispararia universalmente e não proporcionaria sinal clínico.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for FAMMM / C: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para FAMMM / CDKN2A. STUB pendente duas-Co-Lead sinalização.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HBV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HBV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on HBsAg+ OR detectable HBV-DNA in patient without HCC. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending nucleos(t)ide analog suppression (per IND-CHRONIC-HBV-PREVENTION-ANTIVIRAL) + AFP+US HCC surveillance q6mo per AASLD protocol. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchor target DIS-HCC. HBV-associated DLBCL/NHL is also documented in literature but with weaker effect-size data than the HCV-NHL link; covered via the broader NHL prevention surveillance bullet in the antiviral indication rationale. Distinct from RF-UNIVERSAL-HBV-REACTIVATION-RISK (existing) which is the treatment-time RF for HBV reactivation during anti-CD20 / chemo.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HCV + HBV: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HCV + HBV coinfection cancer prevention. Higher severity (critical) than either mono-infection RF — coinfection carries documented synergistic HCC risk AND DAA-cure-induced HBV reactivation risk that requires combination antiviral. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending concurrent DAA + nucleos(t)ide analog + intensified HCC surveillance (US + AFP q4-6mo, more frequent than the q6mo cadence for either mono-infection). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-HCC. NHL prevention (HCV-driven) continues to be a secondary benefit; tracked via prose in the combined-antiviral indication rationale. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HCV-NHL-PREVENTION-OPPORTUNITY and RF-CHRONIC-HBV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (individual mono-infection RFs). When coinfection trigger fires, this RF takes precedence over the two individual RFs (higher priority).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HHV-8-dri: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HHV-8-driven malignancy prevention. Fires on HHV-8 seropositivity in HIV+, transplant, or other immunocompromised host without confirmed Kaposi sarcoma / MCD / PEL. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending immune restoration (ART for HIV+; transplant-immunosuppression rebalance) + mucocutaneous + oral + GI / lymph-node surveillance. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-KAPOSI. MCD and PEL are HHV-8-driven but not yet authored as distinct Disease entities — covered via the prose surveillance rationale in the indication for now. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (existing) — that is HIV-as-RF; this is HHV-8-positivity-as-RF (the co-factor that turns HIV-related immunocompromise into Kaposi risk specifically).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV + HBV: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV + HBV coinfection cancer prevention. Higher severity (critical) than mono-infection HBV RF — coinfection carries documented accelerated-fibrosis + elevated HCC risk AND a hard constraint on antiviral selection (tenofovir-based ART mandatory; entecavir monotherapy contraindicated). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending tenofovir-based ART (covers both viruses simultaneously) + AASLD HCC surveillance q6mo. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-HCC. HIV-driven AIDS-defining malignancies (Kaposi sarcoma via HHV-8 reactivation, NHL, cervical) are covered separately via RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION and RF-CHRONIC-HHV8-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HBV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION and RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (individual mono-infection RFs). When coinfection trigger fires, this RF takes precedence (higher priority) and the indication enforces tenofovir-based ART selection.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on positive HIV serology in patient without AIDS-defining or HIV-associated malignancy. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending durable ART suppression (per IND-CHRONIC-HIV-PREVENTION-ART) + cancer screening cadence (annual anal cytology in MSM/HIV+; q3-yearly cervical Pap in WLHIV; opportunistic Kaposi/oral hairy leukoplakia visual screening). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS as the canonical HIV-associated NHL. KS, cervical, anal, Hodgkin, HCC are also HIV-associated; covered via screening recommendations in the ART indication rationale rather than discrete Disease anchors (until DIS-KAPOSI etc. land in v0.2-A authoring backlog).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPRC. STU: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para HPRC. STUB pendente de duas-Co-Lead sinalização.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on persistent high-risk HPV positivity OR incomplete/absent vaccination in age-eligible individual. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending vaccination (Gardasil-9) and/or risk-group-appropriate screening cadence (cervical: USPSTF Pap+HPV co-test q5y ages 30-65; anal: HRA + cytology q1y in MSM/HIV+/post-transplant). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CERVICAL and DIS-ANAL-SCC. Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma and vulvar/vaginal/penile not yet in KB — v0.2-A authoring backlog.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HTLV-1-dr: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para prevenção de ATLL impulsionada pelo HTLV-1. Ao contrário do VHC/HBV/H. pylori, não há nenhum regime curativo — a intervenção é vigilância + prevenção de transmissão, não cura. STUB pendente Co-Lead revisão. Contexto geográfico: regiões endémicas do HTV-1 incluem Japão (sudoeste), bacia do Caribe, partes da África Subsaariana, partes de América do Sul, Oriente Médio. Ucrânia é de baixa prevalência; este FR é mais relevante para pacientes da diáspora ou aqueles com viagens/origem de regiões endêmicas.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for I-131 the: Prevention-persona RedFlag for I-131 therapeutic-dose lifetime cumulative exposure. Surveillance: CBC q12mo for leukemia signal (sensitivity modest); breast surveillance per general-population USPSTF unless additional risk factors; oral + salivary symptom awareness. Highest-impact preventive intervention is hydration + lemon-juice sialagogue during I-131 administration (reduces salivary gland uptake) — retrospectively non-actionable for prior exposure. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for MASLD/NAF: Prevention-persona RedFlag for MASLD/NAFLD HCC risk. Cirrhotic MASLD meets AASLD HCC-surveillance threshold (US ± AFP q6mo). Non-cirrhotic advanced fibrosis is a gray zone — closer hepatology follow-up but not yet routine surveillance. Major actionable lever: weight loss + cardiometabolic management. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for NF1 confi: Prevention-persona RedFlag for NF1 confirmed-carrier / clinical- diagnostic-criteria-met cohort. Multi-organ surveillance: pediatric ophthalmology q6-12mo to age 8 (optic glioma); whole-body MRI for MPNST surveillance + symptom-driven biopsy of growing/painful/ neurologically-symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas; women: annual mammography from age 30, MRI from age 30-50. STUB pending two-Co- Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for O. viverr: Prevention-persona RedFlag for O. viverrini-driven cholangiocarcinoma prevention. Fires on any documented exposure history with confirmatory testing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending praziquantel (if active infection) + lifelong hepatobiliary surveillance (US + CA 19-9 q12mo from age 40 in heavily-exposed cohorts). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA. Northeast Thailand has the world's highest cholangiocarcinoma incidence (up to 90 per 100K) — attributable fraction in endemic regions exceeds 50%. Geographic context: relevant for Mekong-region diaspora, refugees, travelers, and adoptees. Companion to RF-CLONORCHIS-CHOLANGIO-PREVENTION (East Asian liver-fluke pathway, biologically similar mechanism).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for PALB2 het: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para portadores heterozigotos PALB2. PAL B2 aborda a penetração do câncer de mama BRCA2 e justifica a vigilância do tipo BRCA com RM da mama anual + mamografia a partir da idade de 30 anos, além da vigilância pancreática (EUS ou RM alternando anualmente a partir de 50 anos, ou 10 anos antes do primeiro PDAC em família) para portador FDR-of-PDAC por consórcio CAPS 2022. Discusão RRSO adiada para o limiar BRCA-estilo dada a penetrança ovárica inferior. STUB pendente de dois-Co-Lead sinal por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for PCOS-anov: Prevention-persona RedFlag for PCOS-anovulation endometrial risk. Separated from the broad reproductive RF for clearer routing — PCOS- specific counseling (progestin restoration, metformin, weight loss) is distinct from generic reproductive-history counseling. Symptom-driven endometrial biopsy in any abnormal bleeding ≥6 months of amenorrhea pre-menopausal OR any post-menopausal bleeding. STUB pending two-Co- Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for RAD51C/RA: Prevention-persona RedFlag for RAD51C/RAD51D heterozygous carriers. Approaches BRCA-level ovarian penetrance — NCCN endorses RRSO at completed childbearing or age 45-50. Breast surveillance: individualised by family history; consider annual MRI in additional- risk subset. Olaparib PARP inhibitor active in RAD51C/D-mutant established ovarian cancer (PROfound + GEN-ALL trials). STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for S. haemat: Prevention-persona RedFlag for S. haematobium-driven bladder SCC prevention. Fires on any documented exposure history with confirmatory testing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending praziquantel (if active infection) + lifetime urinary surveillance (urinalysis q6-12mo, cytology + cystoscopy for any new hematuria). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-UROTHELIAL. S. haematobium-driven bladder cancers are predominantly SCC histology (distinct from urothelial / transitional cell carcinoma that dominates Western cohorts) — engine surfaces this distinction in the prevention rationale prose. Geographic context: Ukraine is non-endemic; this RF is relevant for patients with diaspora / refugee / travel / origin history from sub-Saharan Africa, Egypt, Sudan, Yemen, parts of South America.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for SDH-defic: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para síndrome de deficiência de SDH. STUB pendente de dois-Co-Lead sinalização.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for active to: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para uso ativo de tabaco. Intervenção modificavel do câncer-risco-fator do maior impacto. Rotas motoras para PreventionPlan recomendando aconselhamento estruturado para cessação + farmacoterapia + triagem pulmonar LDCT se elegível USPSTF. STUB pendente dois-Clínica-Co-Lead sinal por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for anthracyc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for anthracycline cumulative dose ≥250 mg/m². Cardio surveillance focus (HF / cardiomyopathy); t-AML surveillance overlap covered by separate RF-IATROGENIC-TOPO2-TAML-PREVENTION. Echo q1-5y depending on risk profile (ASCO/COG-LTFU cadence). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending baseline + serial echo + BNP. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for aromatic-: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para aromática-aminas → prevenção do câncer de bexiga urotelial. Fogos na exposição documentada ocupacional. âncora DIS-UROTHELIAL preferiu, mas usando DIS-HCC como retaguarda se não em KB neste ramo. STUB pendente dois-Clínica-Co-Lead sinal por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic E: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic ETS exposure (household / workplace ≥10y). IARC Group 1 + US Surgeon General-confirmed cause of lung cancer in non-smokers. risk_category=occupational is closest enum match — schema lacks an explicit 'environmental' enum. Distinct from active-smoking RF. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending exposure elimination (cohabitant smoking cessation / workplace smoke-free policy enforcement / personal mitigation) + USPSTF screening eligibility check + symptom-triggered evaluation. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic P: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para exposição crônica ao IPP ≥10y. Rotas motoras para PreventionPlan recomenda (1) indicação-revisão + desprescrição onde o IPP já não é necessário (escenatório mais comum), (2) gastrina em jejum + cromogranina A em coorte com indicação persistente de supressão de ácido, (3) EGD com biopsias corpo/fundo em aqueles com gastrina elevada ou sintomas; vigilância EGDE q3-5y se gastrite atrófica ou hiperplasia ECL documentada. Anclado ao DIS-GASTRIC (neto gástrico e adenocarcinoma derivado de atrófica-gastrite, ambas as doenças do corpo gástrico); desfechos específicos do NE transportados na prosa indicativa. STUB pendente sinalização bi-clinical-Co-Lead por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic a: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic anti-TNF biologic exposure ≥3y in pediatric / adolescent / young-adult IBD cohort. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) EBV serology baseline in young adults, (2) B-symptom + lymphadenopathy awareness, (3) annual skin examination (synergistic with concomitant thiopurine + UV), (4) periodic shared-decision discussion of combination- therapy step-down where IBD activity allows (anti-TNF monotherapy has favourable cancer signal vs combination with thiopurine), (5) vaccination catch-up (HPV, HBV, influenza, pneumococcal). Severity = minor — absolute attributable risk in anti-TNF monotherapy is small; the meaningful signal is the combination- with-thiopurine HSTCL warning specifically in pediatric / young- adult cohort, addressed via combination-step-down counseling. Anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS + DIS-HSTCL. STUB pending two-Clinical- Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic i: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic inorganic arsenic exposure via drinking water >10 µg/L (WHO + US EPA MCL). IARC Group 1 carcinogen with established urothelial, lung, and non-melanoma skin cancer etiology. Anchored to DIS-UROTHELIAL per task brief; lung + skin surfaced via relevant_diseases. risk_category=occupational is closest enum match. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending water source change / filtration + intensified screening for affected organs. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic o: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para exposição ultravioleta ocupacional ≥10y em latitudes de alto índice UV. Grupo IARC 1 UV solar. Distinção de RF-LIFESTYLE-UV-EXPOSURE-PREVENTION mais ampla (que cobre camas de bronzeamento + história de queimaduras solares + UV recreativo). Anclado ao DIS-BCC por ficha de tarefa (pele mais próxima DIS para UV-NMSC). Rotas motoras para PreventionPlan recomendando aconselhamento fotoproteção + exame clínico da pele cadença + auto-exame de pele paciente + balanço de vitamina D. STUB pendente de sinalização de duas-Clínica-Co-Lead por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic p: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para pancreatite crônica → PDAC. Pancreatites hereditárias traz maior risco (~40-50% de vida). STUB pendente de sinalização de duas-Co-Lead.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic r: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic residential PM2.5 >35 µg/m³ annual average (WHO 2021 IT-1). IARC Group 1 outdoor air pollution + PM. Population-attributable fraction modest individually but large absolute burden in high-exposure regions including industrial Ukraine + during war-related fire / debris events. risk_category=occupational is the closest enum match — schema lacks an explicit 'environmental' enum (§20 ratification pending). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending exposure reduction + USPSTF lung-cancer screening eligibility + symptom-triggered evaluation. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic ≥: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic ≥3y post-transplant immunosuppression cohort. Engine routes to PreventionPlan with long-cycle surveillance cadence appropriate to the chronic cohort (vs the acute-window EBV-DNA cadence in the new-transplant RF). Distinct from RF-IATROGENIC-TRANSPLANT-IMMUNOSUPPRESSION- PREVENTION (which covers acute / new-transplant window). Both RFs may fire simultaneously in the early-chronic window (1-3y post-transplant) — engine routes to both surveillance tracks, render layer deduplicates overlapping recommendations. Anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS as the primary lymphoma anchor (late- onset PTLD histology more DLBCL-like; DIS-PTLD as the canonical early-onset EBV-driven entity). Multiple cancer types listed in relevant_diseases reflect the broad cumulative-risk profile of the chronic cohort. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for combined: Prevention-persona RedFlag for combined HRT exposure ≥5y. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) shared-decision discussion of risk-benefit (vasomotor symptoms, bone-density preservation vs breast / VTE / cardiovascular risks), (2) lowest-effective-dose + shortest-duration principle per NAMS / ACOG, (3) breast surveillance per USPSTF cadence — supplemental imaging not recommended on HRT alone (density-related supplemental imaging is a separate axis), (4) symptom-prompted endometrial workup (any abnormal bleeding → TVUS + biopsy) for women on sequential/cyclic combined or with intact uterus on any HRT, (5) annual GYN exam. Distinct from RF-IATROGENIC-TAMOXIFEN-ENDOMETRIAL-PREVENTION (different mechanism: SERM with partial endometrial agonism). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.

Prevenção-persona RedFlag para combinação baixa ingestão de cálcio + deficiência de vitamina D. WCRF/AICR prova provável para cálcio e CRC; IARC sinal agrupado para status de vitaminaD. Evidência RCT para suplementação é misturada em doses populacionais — aconselhamento enfatiza ingesta/repleção adequada não farmacológica dosagem. Rotas motoras para PreventionPlan recomendando aconsselhamento dietético + repleção de vitaminad D + triagem de CRC por USPSTF. STUB pendente de sinal de duas-Clínica-Co-Lead por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for cumulativ: Prevention-persona RedFlag for cumulative hormonal-contraception exposure ≥10y, iatrogenic-axis only (exposure-as-risk). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending HPV co-test on schedule per ASCCP / USPSTF, age-appropriate mammographic screening per USPSTF, attentive symptom history (breast lump, abnormal bleeding). Severity minor — absolute risk increment small, effect on breast cancer attenuates after stop. Distinct from RF-REPRODUCTIVE-OCP-LONG-TERM (balanced risk-benefit counseling, see §20 reproductive bucket). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for endometri: Prevention-persona RedFlag for endometriosis-associated ovarian cancer risk. NO routine population-screening tool exists (CA-125 + TVUS not recommended for general or endometriosis screening per NCCN/USPSTF). Counseling: symptom awareness; consider risk-reducing salpingectomy at completed childbearing or at hysterectomy for benign indications; BSO reserved for those with additional risk factors. STUB pending two-Co- Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for heavy alc: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para uso de álcool pesado. Rotas motoras para PrevençõesPlaneia recomendando aconselhamento estruturado de cessação/moderação + farmacoterapia + rastreamento apropriado do câncer (endoscopia esofágica para vigilância do câncer de mama de alto risco para mulheres). STUB pendente bi-Clínica-Co-Lead sinal por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for high cumu: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para alta exposição cumulativa UV. Classificação IARC Grupo 1 para camas bronzeadoras (2009). NCCN Melanoma + diretrizes AAD suportam aconselhamento de proteção UV + auto-exame cutâneo + cadença clínica exame cutênico. Rotas motoras para PreventionPlan recomendando proteção solar + vigilância cutária. STUB pendente sinalização de duas-Clínica-Co-Lead por CHARTER §6.1 modo dev.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for high-pari: Prevention-persona RedFlag for high-parity cervical risk amplifier in HPV-positive women. Counseling: adherence to cervical screening per USPSTF/WHO age-and-method schedule; catch-up HPV vaccination through age 45 per ACIP shared-decision; smoking cessation (synergistic risk). STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for in-utero: Prevention-persona RedFlag for in-utero DES exposure. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending annual gynecologic exam with speculum + bimanual + careful palpation of vaginal walls (specific technique for DES daughters per ACOG), colposcopy with vaginal + cervical staining for early detection of CCA, cervical cytology / HPV co-test on routine cadence, breast surveillance per age- appropriate USPSTF cadence. Cohort is aging — bimodal-risk window extends past 40y; surveillance does NOT stop at any age cutoff. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-VULVAR-VAGINAL-SCC (closest existing Disease entity for vaginal-tract anchor) + DIS-CERVICAL. DES- associated cancer is histologically clear-cell adenocarcinoma — NOT yet authored as a distinct DIS-VAGINAL-CLEAR-CELL entity; histology-specific surveillance considerations carried via the indication prose. Future authoring of DIS-VAGINAL-CLEAR-CELL recommended. Distinct from RF-IATROGENIC-LONG-TERM-HRMNL-CONTRACEPTION- PREVENTION (post-natal hormonal exposure, exposure-as-cofactor). This is a one-time in-utero developmental exposure — surveillance cohort is closed (no new DES daughters); known existing cohort remains at lifelong elevated risk.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for late-firs: Prevention-persona RedFlag for late-first-pregnancy + short-breastfeeding combination. Modest individual effect sizes; cumulative effect non-trivial. Cannot retroactively modify primary trigger (timing of reproductive events) — counseling is forward-looking (encourage breastfeeding when feasible in subsequent pregnancies) + tightened breast cancer screening. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for long-term: Prevenção-persona RedFlag para uso combinado de longo prazo OCP ≥10y. Perfil de câncer misto — aumento de risco modesto (peito, cervical com-HPV) E proteção substancial (ovário, endometrial). Rotas motoras para PreventionPlan recomendando indicação de CONSEGUIMENTO-BALANCE, não alerta de risco unidirecional. Critical que torna a camada apresentar painel de risco-benefício completo. STUB pendente de sinalização de dois-Clínico-Co-Lead por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.

Prevenção-persona RedFlag para exposição a dose baixa de longa duração MTX (RA, psoríase, IBD). Vigilância: tratamento de baixas doses para linfadenopatia inexplicável, sintomas B, organomegalia, massa — retirada de MTx + observar 8-12 semanas primeiro (~50% regressão); persistente → DLBCL-estilo. exame de pele anualmente. STUB pendente de sinalização de duas-Co-Lead por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.

Prevenção-persona RedFlag para exposição a longo prazo ≥3y tiopurina (azatioprina / 6-MP). Rotas motoras para PreventionPlan recomenda (1) exame anual de pele do corpo inteiro por dermatologista + aconselhamento agressivo de proteção solar, (2) verificação de serologia do EBV em adultos jovens pré-inicialização (evitar início em homens jovens seronegativos do EOV por ECCO 2019), (3) revisão anual do sintômeo B + linfadenopatia, (4) discussão de decisão partilhada da continuação da indicação vs alternativas (MTX para AR, biológicos para o IBD) no ano 5, (5) Apanhamento da vacinação contra o HPV, quando aplicável. Anclado ao DIS-DLBCL-NOS (linfoma) + DIS-BCC (ancora mais próxima do câncer de pele para CSC e BCC). STUB pendente de sinalização de duas-Clínica-Co-Lead por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.

Prevention-persona RedFlag for long-term ≥5y calcineurin-inhibitor exposure (cyclosporine or tacrolimus). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) annual or q6mo whole-body skin exam by dermatologist (q6mo if any prior skin cancer), (2) aggressive sun-protection counseling, (3) HHV-8 awareness in endemic cohorts + KS surveillance (skin, oral, GI), (4) HPV vaccination catch-up if transplant context, (5) shared-decision discussion with transplant team of switch to mTOR inhibitor (sirolimus / everolimus) in patients with cumulative skin- cancer burden — CONVERT + ProSparc evidence: mTOR-switch reduces new SCC. Anchored to DIS-KAPOSI + DIS-BCC. KEYNOTE-158 (Shapira-Frommer, Gynecol Oncol 2022) evaluated pembrolizumab monotherapy in previously treated advanced vulvar SCC (n=101): durable responses (ORR 10.9% overall, median DOR 20.4 months among responders) occurred in BOTH PD-L1-positive (ORR 9.5%, n=84) and PD-L1-negative (ORR 28.6%, n=7 — small subgroup, wide CI) patients. CPS≥1 is therefore NOT a validated hard predictive cutoff for vulvar SCC pembrolizumab response, unlike the CPS≥1 FDA-label requirement for cervical cancer (KEYNOTE-826). Primary IO resistance is operationally d: Primary IO resistance is operationally distinct from acquired resistance (PD after initial response >6 months). SITC consensus (Kluger 2020) defines primary resistance as PD within 6 months of IO start. Subsequent options vary by tumor: melanoma — BRAF/MEKi if V600E, T-VEC, TIL therapy at trial centers, IL-2; NSCLC — docetaxel ± ramucirumab, ADC if HER2/TROP2; urothelial — enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab combination remains active even after IO-mono PD per EV-302; RCC — cabozantinib monotherapy or lenvatinib + everolimus. IO-rechallenge is generally not standard but may be considered after >6 months treatment-free + non-PD discontinuation reason.

Primary Sjögren's syndrome (chronic autoimmune exocrinopathy with characteristic anti-Ro/SSA ± anti-La/SSB autoantibodies and histologic focal lymphocytic infiltration of minor salivary glands; EULAR/ACR 2016 classification criteria) in an individual without a current lymphoma diagnosis. The strongest hematologic-cancer risk factor among rheumatic diseases — ~15-20x relative risk for marginal zone (MALT) lymphoma, predominantly arising in parotid and lacrimal glands, with lifetime incidence ~5-10%. Risk concentrated in patients with persistent parotid swelling, palpable purpura, cryoglobulinemia, low C4 complement, monoclonal gammopathy, lymph- node enlargement, or high EULAR Sjögren's Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI). Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) — confirmed by characteristic cholangiographic findings on MRCP or ERCP (multifocal intra-/extra- hepatic biliary strictures with intervening dilatation, beaded appearance) and/or liver biopsy (concentric periductal fibrosis, onion-skin pattern). Includes PSC-IBD subgroup (very high risk for both CRC and cholangiocarcinoma) and PSC with dominant biliary stricture (additional cholangiocarcinoma risk requiring focused diagnostic workup). No current cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder cancer, or HCC diagnosis. PSC is the strongest known risk factor for cholangiocarcinoma — lifetime risk ~10-15% (vs ~0.01% in general population); annual incidence ~0.5-1.5% per year.
