Seqüência de fase — 0,16 mg → 0,8 mg → 48 mg — com prednisolone profilática 100 mg × 4 dias em torno de cada dose suprime o SRC de qualquer grau até ~50% (predominantemente Grau 1-2; G≥3 ~3%) por EPCORE NHL-1. Entidade sub-regime autoriada separadamente para possibilitar reutilização em DLBCL/FL/indicações futuras e para fornecer uma única entidade para o render para fazer superfície do ciclo-1 de monitoramento hospitalar + padrão de profilaxia corticosteróide. Combinar com esquema parental (REGIMEN-EPCORITAMAB-MONO-DLBcl-3L) para curso completo. Registro bibliográfico SRC-EPCORE-NHL-1-THIEBLEMONT-2023 está disponível; o linking de alegações clínicas requer dupla assinatura clínica.
Standalone authoring of the obinutuzumab: Standalone authoring of the obinutuzumab single-dose pretreatment sub-regimen used to pre-deplete circulating CD20+ B-cells 7 days before glofitamab cycle 1 day 1. Mechanistically reduces CRS risk by shrinking the bispecific T-cell-engager substrate at first exposure; in NP30179 the combined obinutuzumab pretreatment + glofitamab step-up + corticosteroid premedication strategy held G≥3 CRS to ~4%. Sub-regimen entity authored separately for reuse across DLBCL / FL / future glofitamab combinations and to allow the renderer to surface the day -7 scheduling requirement as a distinct phase in patient-facing plans. Pair with parent schedule (REGIMEN-GLOFITAMAB-MONO-DLBCL-3L) starting 7 days later. Bibliographic record SRC-NP30179-DICKINSON-2022 is available; clinical claim linkage requires dual clinical sign-off.
Standard 12-week varenicline course is t: Standard 12-week varenicline course is the most effective single-agent tobacco-cessation pharmacotherapy (USPSTF + AHCPR). Set quit date day 8 of treatment (~end of titration). Extension to 24 weeks improves long-term abstinence in patients abstinent at 12 weeks. Counsel patients on neuropsychiatric monitoring (EAGLES 2016 reassured but residual caution).
Standard 1L cytoreduction for high-risk: Standard 1L cytoreduction for high-risk PV (age >60 OR prior thrombosis) AND high-risk ET (same criteria). Targets: - PV: Hct <45% (mainstay; CYTO-PV trial), platelets <400K - ET: platelets <400-450K Phlebotomy is the foundation in PV (with HU layered for cytoreduction); ASA at low dose unless contraindicated (extreme thrombocytosis with acquired vWD = relative contraindication). STUB — requires clinical co-lead signoff before publication.
Standard 1L for AML unfit for intensive: Standard 1L for AML unfit for intensive 7+3 (VIALE-A: median OS 14.7 vs 9.6 mo for aza alone). TLS prophylaxis MANDATORY for first ramp cycle (5-week ramp not used in AML — accelerated 3-day ramp instead). Strong CYP3A4 inhibitor co-administration (azole prophylaxis) requires venetoclax dose reduction. STUB — requires clinical co-lead signoff before publication.
Standard 1L for MDS-HR (and bridging to: Standard 1L for MDS-HR (and bridging to alloHCT in eligible patients). Azacitidine and decitabine functionally equivalent; choice often local. Do NOT discontinue before cycle 6 unless overt progression — response is delayed. Ven+aza in HR-MDS is increasingly used (off-label extrapolation from VIALE-A AML data; no Phase-3 HR-MDS-specific RCT). STUB — requires clinical co-lead signoff before publication.
Standard 1L for R/M HNSCC with CPS ≥1 (t: Standard 1L for R/M HNSCC with CPS ≥1 (the majority of HNSCC). Locally advanced (curable) HNSCC routes to concurrent cisplatin + RT or surgery + adjuvant — separate algorithm not yet authored. HPV+ oropharyngeal R/M handled identically (no de-escalation in recurrent setting). Reuses pembrolizumab + cisplatin + carboplatin + 5-FU drug entities.
Standard 1L for advanced / metastatic GI: Standard 1L for advanced / metastatic GIST with imatinib-sensitive genotype (KIT exon 11 ~50%; KIT exon 9 ~10% — escalate to 800 mg; PDGFRA non-D842V exon 18; PDGFRA exon 12/14). NOT effective in PDGFRA D842V (use avapritinib 1L) or in SDH-deficient KIT/PDGFRA-WT GIST. B2222 / Demetri NEJM 2002 ORR ~67%; long-term PFS ~24 mo exon 11 vs ~12 mo exon 9. Genotype testing prior to 1L is mandatory per NCCN.
Standard 1L for fit transplant-eligible: Padrão 1L para MCL elegível para transplante de ajuste (idade <65, ECOG 0-1). Protocolo nórdico ou estilo LYMA. Contribuição principal: HiDAC + consolidação autoSCT + manutenção R melhorou drasticamente PFS (mediana >7-8 anos vs ~3 anos em R-CHOP em monoterapia). Risco de cardiotoxicidade + toxicidade cumulativa HiDac - seleção de aptidão crítica.
Standard 1L for fit-for-intensive AML. A: Standard 1L for fit-for-intensive AML. Add midostaurin if FLT3-ITD/TKD+ (RATIFY: improved 4-y OS 51% vs 44%). Day-14 BM check at end of induction; if blasts persist → re-induction. Consolidation HiDAC 3 g/m² q12h d1, 3, 5 for 3-4 cycles in young fit favorable / intermediate-risk; alloHCT for adverse-risk in CR1. STUB — requires clinical co-lead signoff before publication.
Standard 1L for low-risk CML chronic pha: Standard 1L for low-risk CML chronic phase, elderly, comorbid patients, or where cost / access is limiting. IRIS established imatinib 400 mg daily; 10-y OS ~83%. ELN 2020 milestones: ≤10% at 3 mo, ≤1% at 6 mo, ≤0.1% (MMR) at 12 mo. PCR monitoring q3mo for first year, then q3-6mo. TFR attempt eligible after ≥3 years on TKI + sustained DMR (MR4.5) ≥2 years per ELN. STUB — requires clinical co-lead signoff before publication.
Standard 1L for low-risk Sokal/EUTOS CML: Standard 1L for low-risk Sokal/EUTOS CML, elderly, or in cost-constrained settings (generics widely available, NSZU-reimbursed in Ukraine). 2nd-gen TKIs (dasatinib, nilotinib, bosutinib) achieve faster deep molecular response but no…
Standard 1L for low/intermediate-risk AP: Standard 1L for low/intermediate-risk APL (Sanz WBC ≤10). APL0406: 2-y EFS 97% vs 86% with ATRA+chemo (AIDA), OS 99% vs 91%, less hematologic toxicity, no anthracycline cardiotoxicity. ATRA initiated IMMEDIATELY at clinical APL suspicion (do NOT wait for cytogenetic confirmation). Daily ECG + electrolyte protocol mandatory during ATO induction. STUB — requires clinical co-lead signoff before publication.
Standard 1L for the imatinib-sensitive G: O padrão 1L para os genótipos GIST sensíveis ao imatinib (~85% de todos os GIST). Reutiliza a linha cruzada REG-IMATINIB-GIST-1L que codifica a regra de escalação de dose do exon 9 do KIT.
Standard 1L for the ~50-100% of advanced: Padrão 1L para o ~50-100% do MTC avançado que é RET-mutante (esporádico ~50% RET M918T; hereditário MEN2 ~100%). Reutiliza doenças cruzadas DRUG-SELPERCATINIB.
Standard 1L induction regimen for transp: Standard 1L induction regimen for transplant-eligible MM (4 cycles before harvest, then ASCT, then 2 cycles consolidation, then lenalidomide maintenance). For transplant-ineligible patients, VRd-lite (8-12 cycles, modified dosing per SWOG S0777) is the preferred 1L triplet. Standard-risk cytogenetics → VRd; high-risk → escalate to D-VRd (REG-DARA-VRD).
Standard 1L regimen for newly-diagnosed: Standard 1L regimen for newly-diagnosed DLBCL NOS for the past 20+ years. ~60% cure rate overall, ~80% for low-IPI / ~55% for high-IPI. HBV screening + entecavir prophylaxis if HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ MANDATORY before first rituximab dose. Echocardiogram (LVEF) baseline + after cumulative dose >300 mg/m². Interim PET-CT after cycles 2-4 helpful for response assessment but doesn't routinely change therapy unless PD seen.
Standard 1L symptom-directed therapy for: Standard 1L symptom-directed therapy for symptomatic PMF (and post-PV/ET MF). COMFORT-I/II: ≥35% spleen-volume reduction in ~42% vs 0.7% placebo; symptom improvement; pooled OS benefit suggested. Does NOT eliminate clone or alter natural history of fibrosis. AlloHCT remains the only curative option for fit intermediate-2 / high-risk patients. Momelotinib (MOMENTUM) preferred if anemia dominant; fedratinib (FREEDOM-2) 2L; pacritinib for severe thrombocytopenia. NEVER abrupt-stop. STUB — requires clinical co-lead signoff before publication.
Standard 2L for SMZL/NMZL after rituxima: Padrão 2L para SMZL/NMZI após falha de monoterapia com rituximab. ORR ~85-90%; mediana da PFS ~3-4 anos. profilaxia PJP ≥6 mo pós-anti-CD20; vigilância da reativação do VHB obrigatória.
Standard 2L mCRC after FOLFOX progressio: Standard 2L mCRC after FOLFOX progression. Adding bevacizumab (TML / ML18147 trial) improves PFS (5.7 vs 4.1 mo) + OS (11.2 vs 9.8 mo, HR 0.81) over FOLFIRI alone. Anti-EGFR (cetuximab or panitumumab) alternative add-on for RAS-WT left-sided patients in 2L if not used in 1L (or if patient progressed on bevacizumab). UGT1A1 testing recommended before high-dose irinotecan use. Cholinergic syndrome vs delayed diarrhea — distinct pathophysiology + management.
Standard 2L+ for R/R FLT3-mutated AML pe: Standard 2L+ for R/R FLT3-mutated AML per ADMIRAL. Bridge to alloHCT for fit candidates achieving CR/CRh — gilteritinib alone is not curative. Continue gilteritinib post-HCT as maintenance (off-label, supported by emerging data MORPHO trial). STUB — pending Co-Lead sign-off.
Standard 2L+ for R/R IDH2-mutated AML pe: Standard 2L+ for R/R IDH2-mutated AML per AG221-AML-001 (FDA approval Aug 2017). Bridge to alloHCT for fit candidates achieving CR/CRh — enasidenib monotherapy is not curative; durable responses in trial were largely consolidated by alloHCT. Differentiation syndrome (~14%) is the signature AE — same dexamethasone protocol as ivosidenib. Hyperbilirubinemia (~80% any grade) is biochemical UGT1A1 inhibition — usually asymptomatic, no dose adjustment unless symptomatic. Bibliographic record SRC-IDHENTIFY is available; SRC-AG221-AML-001 remains a source gap. STUB — pending Co-Lead sign-off.
Standard 2L+ for R/R KMT2A-rearranged AM: Standard 2L+ for R/R KMT2A-rearranged AML per AUGMENT-101 (FDA approval Nov 2024). Bridge to alloHCT for fit candidates achieving CR/CRh — revumenib monotherapy is not curative; durable responses in trial were largely consolidated by alloHCT. Differentiation syndrome (~16%) is the signature AE — same dexamethasone protocol as ivosidenib / enasidenib. QTc prolongation requires baseline + serial ECG. Bibliographic record SRC-AUGMENT-101 is available; clinical claim linkage requires dual clinical sign-off. STUB — pending Co-Lead sign-off.
Standard 3-dose adult schedule (Engerix-: Standard 3-dose adult schedule (Engerix-B / Recombivax HB / PreHevbrio): 0, 1, 6 months. Each dose 1.0 mL IM in deltoid. Pediatric schedule (Engerix-B / Recombivax HB): Birth dose (within 24 h of birth), then 1-2 months, then 6-18 months. Each dose 0.5 mL IM (anterolateral thigh in infants). Two-dose adult schedule (Heplisav-B, CpG-adjuvanted, age ≥18): 0 and 1 month. Each dose 0.5 mL IM in deltoid. Three-dose adult schedule (PreHevbrio, tri-antigen, age ≥18): 0, 1, 6 months. Each dose 1.0 mL IM in deltoid. Hemodialysis / immunocompromised: double-dose (Engerix-B 40 mcg × 4 doses at 0, 1, 2, 6 months; Recombivax HB 40 mcg × 3 doses). Standard 3-dose schedule (FDA / EMA hist: Standard 3-dose schedule (FDA / EMA historical labeling, age 9-25 F): 0, 1, 6 months. Each dose 0.5 mL IM in deltoid (preferred). WHO position 2017+: 2-dose schedule (0 and 6-12 months) acceptable for girls <15 y who are immunocompetent (single-dose alternative schedule under continued study in WHO/IARC SAGE 2022+). Catch-up: complete the 3-dose series in those who started but did not complete; do not restart if interrupted. Hepatic / renal impairment: no dose adjustment. Pregnancy: avoid initiating series in pregnancy (insufficient data, not a known teratogen); complete after delivery. Lactation: compatible.
Standard FLT3-ITD/TKD AML 1L (RATIFY tri: Padrão FLT3-ITD/TKD AML 1L (estudo RATIFY: melhora da SO vs placebo quando adicionado a 7+3 + HiDAC). Tome com alimentos para maximizar a biodisponibilidade. profilaxia antiemética essencial. Não reembolsado na Ucrânia — constrição de acesso maior; gilteritinib (r/r com agente único) e quizartinib também FLT3.

Standard FLT3-ITD/TKD AML 1L (RATIFY trial: improved OS vs placebo when added to 7+3 + HiDAC). Take with food to maximize bioavailability. Antiemetic prophylaxis essential. Not Ukraine-reimbursed — major access constraint; gilteritinib…
Standard H2 component of chemotherapy pr: Standard H2 component of chemotherapy premedication, paired with H1 antihistamine (diphenhydramine) and corticosteroid (dexamethasone). Particularly important before paclitaxel (Cremophor vehicle hyper- sensitivity), rituximab, daratumumab, and other monoclonal antibodies with significant infusion reaction rates. Combined H1 + H2 blockade is empirically superior to H1 alone for prevention of mild-to-moderate hypersensitivity reactions (Lieberman-Goodyear, 2010). NEVER a substitute for epinephrine in true anaphylaxis — H1 + H2 + steroid treats pruritus, urticaria, mild bronchospasm, but does not reverse hypotension or upper airway edema. Famotidine preferred over cimetidine in oncology because of clean DDI profile (cimetidine inhibits multiple CYPs causing exposure increases of warfarin, theophylline, phenytoin, TKIs, vincristine — major hazard); ranitidine withdrawn worldwide 2019-2020 for NDMA contamination. CRITICAL: H2 antagonists raise gastric pH → reduce absorption of pH-dependent oral oncology agents (dasatinib, erlotinib, gefitinib, dabigatran, atazanavir) — separate by 2-10 h or substitute / time TKI dose. Standard NGS; ctDNA acceptable for monit: NGS padrão; ctDNA aceitável para monitorização
Standard NGS; tipifarnib enrolment uses: NGS padrão; a matrícula em tipifarnib utiliza limiar VAF ≥20% em alguns ensaios
Standard PPI-clarithromycin-amoxicillin: Standard PPI-clarithromycin-amoxicillin triple therapy for H. pylori eradication. Preferred only in regions with clarithromycin resistance ≤15%. In Ukraine and most of Eastern Europe, clarithromycin resistance is >15% — Maastricht VI/Florence Consensus 2022 recommends PBMT (REG-HP-BISMUTH-QUADRUPLE) as first-line instead.
Standard R-CHOP component. Premedication: Standard R-CHOP component. Premedication: 5-HT3 antagonist + dexamethasone. Mesna NOT routinely needed at R-CHOP doses (750 mg/m²) but mandatory for high-dose conditioning (>1500 mg/m²).
Standard TLS prophylaxis when initiating: Profilaxia padrão TLS ao iniciar a quimioimunoterapia em pacientes com alta carga tumoral. Comece 24-48 horas antes da terapêutica.
Standard VTE prophylaxis for lenalidomid: Standard VTE prophylaxis for lenalidomide-treated MM patients without additional VTE risk factors. For higher-risk patients (prior VTE, immobility, central venous catheter, active disease at induction) switch to LMWH (enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily) or apixaban. Hold aspirin if platelets <50K.

Standard adjunct for bronchospasm compon: Standard adjunct for bronchospasm component of anaphylaxis, chemotherapy infusion reactions, and CAR-T cytokine release syndrome — given concurrently with epinephrine (epinephrine remains the FIRST-LINE for true anaphylaxis with hypotension or upper airway edema). Nebulized 2.5-5 mg q20min × 3 then q1-4h is standard for moderate-severe bronchospasm. Critical: salbutamol does NOT reverse hypotension or upper airway edema — if these are present, epinephrine IM thigh is mandatory and urgent. Add ipratropium 500 µg nebulized if bronchospasm refractory or severe (combined β2 + muscarinic blockade). For bronchospasm during paclitaxel, rituximab, or monoclonal antibody infusions: stop infusion, administer salbutamol nebulized, diphenhydramine + famotidine + steroid as supportive — escalate to epinephrine if hypotension / upper airway involvement / no response in 5-10 min. Avoid in patients with cardiomyopathy / serious arrhythmia (QT-prolonging chemotherapy regimens particularly — TKIs, arsenic trioxide). Tachycardia and hypokalemia are dose-related — monitor in continuous nebulization. Ukraine: cheap, ubiquitous, NSZU-covered.
Standard adjunct for chemotherapy infusi: Standard adjunct for chemotherapy infusion reactions and severe anaphylaxis — given AFTER epinephrine IM (epinephrine is first-line, no substitute). Hydrocortisone's onset is delayed (4-6 h) so it prevents biphasic anaphylaxis recurrence rather than treating the acute event. Premedication for chemotherapy (e.g., taxanes, rituximab, daratumumab): typically dexamethasone 20 mg IV is used rather than hydrocortisone — dex is more potent (×30) per mg, has longer duration, lacks mineralocorticoid effect (less fluid retention), and dosing schedule is established. Hydrocortisone preferred over dex / methylprednisolone for: (1) adrenal insufficiency / crisis (mineralocorticoid activity matches physiological need); (2) septic shock with vasopressor refractoriness (300 mg/day approximately physiologic stress dose); (3) acute high-dose adjunct for refractory infusion reaction where mineralocorticoid effect supports hemodynamics. Single bolus of 100-200 mg has minimal long-term consequences — no taper needed for ≤3 days of acute use. Ukraine: cheap, ubiquitous, NSZU- covered.
Standard adjuvant for stage III colon, a: Adjuvante padrão para o cólon estágio III, também estágio II de alto risco (T4 / invasão linfovascular / < 12 LN amostrado / pouco diff). Metástase 1L para o RAS-WT lado direito OR RAS mutante + bev (combinado com bevacizumab) — ver Indicação entradas para lógica biológica-add-on.
Standard adult dose: 500 mg PO once dail: Standard adult dose: 500 mg PO once daily, continuous, with or without food (avoid high-fat meals — increase exposure ~25%). Treatment continued until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Indication-specific notes: - Cholangiocarcinoma: 500 mg PO once daily continuous (28-day cycle for accounting; no scheduled break). - AML monotherapy (R/R or 1L unfit): 500 mg PO once daily continuous; minimum 6 months of therapy recommended to allow differentiation response (median time-to-CR ~2 months). - AML + azacitidine (AGILE): ivosidenib 500 mg PO daily + azacitidine 75 mg/m² SC/IV days 1–7 of each 28-day cycle. Standard adult dose: 800 mg PO once dail: Standard adult dose: 800 mg PO once daily continuous, taken on an empty stomach (≥1 hour before or ≥2 hours after a meal — food significantly increases exposure and toxicity risk). Dose reductions to 400 mg then 200 mg for grade 3-4 toxicity or hepatic AE per labelling. Treatment continued until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Hepatic monitoring schedule (per FDA boxed warning): LFTs at baseline, weeks 3, 5, 7, 9, then monthly through month 4, then periodically. Hold for ALT >3× ULN; permanently discontinue for ALT >8× ULN or concurrent ALT >3× ULN with bilirubin >2× ULN. Standard adult monotherapy: 240 mg IV q2: Standard adult monotherapy: 240 mg IV q2w OR 480 mg IV q4w (over 30 min). Pediatric melanoma adjuvant (≥12 yrs, ≥40 kg): 240 mg q2w; <40 kg: 3 mg/kg q2w. With ipilimumab (1L melanoma, RCC, MSI-H CRC): nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg q3w × 4 doses, then nivolumab 240 mg q2w or 480 mg q4w maintenance. CheckMate-649 (gastric 1L + chemo): 360 mg q3w with chemo or 240 mg q2w. CheckMate-577 (adjuvant esophageal post-CROSS without pCR): 240 mg q2w × 16 wks, then 480 mg q4w to total 1 year. Treatment until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or specified duration (1 yr adjuvant; 2 yrs metastatic in some indications).
Standard adult: 200 mg IV q3 weeks OR 40: Standard adult: 200 mg IV q3 weeks OR 400 mg IV q6 weeks (over 30 min). Pediatric: 2 mg/kg (up to 200 mg) IV q3w. Treatment continued until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or 24 months in most solid-tumor indications (35 cycles q3w). Adjuvant melanoma: 1 year (KEYNOTE-054). Neoadjuvant + adjuvant TNBC (KEYNOTE-522): 200 mg q3w × 8 cycles with chemo, then 9 cycles adjuvant. Neoadjuvant + adjuvant NSCLC (KEYNOTE-671): 200 mg q3w × 4 cycles with platinum-doublet, then 13 cycles adjuvant. Combination doses unchanged when paired with chemo, lenvatinib, axitinib, or trastuzumab.
Standard antibacterial prophylaxis in hi: Standard antibacterial prophylaxis in high-risk febrile neutropenia per IDSA / NCCN: anticipated ANC <100/µL ≥7 days (HSCT conditioning, AML induction, high-dose chemo for relapsed leukemia/lymphoma). Started day of conditioning / induction, continued through ANC recovery (>500/µL or marrow recovery). The Gram-positive enhancement vs ciprofloxacin (esp. viridans streptococcal mucositis-bacteremia prevention) is the rationale. Trade-offs: selects fluoroquinolone- resistant organisms over time (rising rates of ciprofloxacin/ levofloxacin-resistant E. coli and viridans streptococci limit benefit at some centers — local antibiogram critical); does NOT prevent invasive fungal infection (separate antifungal prophylaxis required — posaconazole, fluconazole). Standard 750 mg dose for pneumonia + Pseudomonas; 500 mg sufficient for FN prophylaxis. Diabetes: severe / fatal hypoglycemia signal — stricter monitoring. Class-wide FDA / EMA 2018 warning: avoid in uncomplicated infections. Ukraine: NSZU-covered for hematology prophylaxis indications; widely available.
Standard antiemetic premedication for mo: Standard antiemetic premedication for moderately/highly emetogenic chemotherapy (e.g., bendamustine).
Standard antifungal prophylaxis in HSCT: Standard antifungal prophylaxis in HSCT — pivotal trial (van Burik CID 2004) demonstrated superiority over fluconazole for invasive fungal infection prevention in HSCT recipients. Also first-line treatment for candidemia and invasive candidiasis (IDSA 2016 echinocandin recommendation). Differentiator from caspofungin: no loading dose, no body-weight adjustment, no hepatic adjustment in moderate impairment, even simpler DDI profile (no clinically meaningful interactions with cyclosporine or tacrolimus — key advantage in HSCT and solid-organ transplant where calcineurin inhibitors are concurrent). Boxed warning regarding hepatic tumors in rat carcinogenicity studies has not translated to human signal in two decades of post-marketing surveillance, but prescribing information warns against unnecessary prolonged use. Same spectrum limitations as caspofungin (no Mucor, no Cryptococcus, fungistatic for Aspergillus). Ukraine: registered, NSZU-covered; preferred echinocandin in HSCT contexts.
Standard backbone for non-squamous NSCLC: Standard backbone for non-squamous NSCLC (KEYNOTE-189: carbo + pem + pembro vs carbo + pem placebo, OS HR 0.49 in PD-L1-all- comers — practice-defining 1L for non-squamous EGFR/ALK-WT NSCLC) and for malignant pleural mesothelioma (EMPHACIS…
Standard bulky-disease definition adapte: Definição padrão de doença voluminosa adaptada a partir das diretrizes para o linfoma de células B.
Standard chemoimmunotherapy regimen for: Standard chemoimmunotherapy regimen for indolent B-cell lymphomas. In HCV-MZL, reserved for cases that are non-responsive to antiviral therapy or have aggressive/bulky disease at presentation requiring immediate cytoreduction.
Standard first-line empirical antibiotic: Standard first-line empirical antibiotic for febrile neutropenia (FN) per IDSA 2010 (Freifeld), ECIL-4, and NCCN — combines pseudomonal coverage, broad anaerobic activity, and acceptable toxicity profile. De-escalate after 48-72 h based on cultures (pip-tazo continued or narrowed to a directed agent). Add vancomycin if MRSA suspected (line infection, skin/soft-tissue source, prior MRSA colonization, hemodynamic instability) — but the pip-tazo + vanco combination has a debated AKI signal in adults (no signal in pediatrics or in CRRT). Common errors: under-dosing in CrCl 40-60 (still use 4.5 g q8h, not q12h), failure to extend infusion in critically ill patients (4-h infusion improves T>MIC), missing the rash → DRESS / SJS conversion early. Sodium load matters in heart failure — 4.5 g q6h delivers ~3 g sodium/ day. Ukraine: widely available; first-line FN empirical agent in hematology centers per local protocols aligned with NCCN/IDSA.
Standard for stage III unresectable post: Standard for stage III unresectable post-concurrent CRT. Pneumonitis G≥2 at end of CRT excludes durva initiation.
Standard for transfusion-dependent del(5: Padrão para transfusão dependente de del(5q) LR-MDS. ~56% alcançar a independência de transfusão RBC (MDS-004); ~20-25% alcançar CR citogenética (perda de clone del( 5q)). Prevenção da gravidez obrigatória (programa REMS/Revlimid). profilaxia VTE obrigatoriedade. Evite a combinação com ESA. STUB — pendente assinatura Co-Lead.
Standard intensification for fit younger: Standard intensification for fit younger transplant-eligible PTCL NOS. Per Nordic NLG-T-01 + retrospective registry data: CHOEP superior to CHOP in younger T-cell patients; alloSCT consolidation in CR1 dramatically improves long-term PFS for poor-risk PTCL NOS (mature data from EBMT registries). AutoSCT alternative considered but generally inferior for PTCL NOS (vs B-cell NHL where autoSCT is durable). RIC alloSCT for older fit; myeloablative for younger. Donor selection critical — sibling > matched unrelated > haploidentical; GVHD prophylaxis individualized.
Standard neoadjuvant for HER2+ stage II-: Standard neoadjuvant for HER2+ stage II-III. pCR rate ~60-65% with TCHP. Path to KATHERINE-eligibility: residual disease post-neoadj → adjuvant T-DM1; pCR → continue trastuzumab + pertuzumab to 1 year total.
Standard of care for myeloma-related bon: Standard of care for myeloma-related bone disease — reduces skeletal- related events and pain. Calcium + vitamin D supplementation mandatory. Comprehensive dental evaluation BEFORE initiation; avoid invasive dental procedures during therapy. Monthly dosing for ≤2 years, then re-evaluate.
Standard of care for premenopausal HR+ a: Standard of care for premenopausal HR+ adjuvant. Switch to AI ± ovarian suppression after 2-5 years often considered. Postmenopausal: AI generally preferred but tamoxifen acceptable when AI contraindicated.
Standard pattern; entecavir/TDF prophyla: Padrão padrão; profilaxia entecavir/TDF de -7d a 12 mo pós-anti-PD-1.
Standard platinum-based chemoimmunothera: Standard platinum-based chemoimmunotherapy per PD-L1 status (pembrolizumab ± carboplatin/paclitaxel or pemetrexed per KEYNOTE-189/024)

Standard platinum-based chemoimmunotherapy per PD-L1 status (pembrolizumab ± carboplatin/paclitaxel or pemetrexed per KEYNOTE-189/024), Enrollment in KRAS G12V-selective inhibitor trials where available (e.g., RMC-6236 expansion cohorts)
Standard pre-anti-CD20 screening; HBV re: Triagem pré-anti-CD20 padrão; reativação do VHB manipulada por RF universal.
Standard salvage for chemosensitive r/r: Resgate padrão para PMBCL r/r quimiosensível. Rituximab + ICE × 2-3 ciclos → avaliação da resposta (PET) → BEAM-condicionamento autoSCT se PR/CR. ~50-60% alcançar remissão durável pós-autoSCT. CAR-T (axi-cel/liso-cel) é alternativa para a recidiva quimiorrefractorial ou pós-AutoSCT . Pembrolizumab também ativo em PMBLC r/R (KEYNOTE-170).
Standard stage III adjuvant. Decision on: Decisão sobre a duração (3 vs 6 mo) por grupo de risco IDEA.
Standard track for AML 1L unfit. Curativ: A via padrão para AML 1L imprópria. O potencial curativo limitado (SG mediana ~ 14 meses); um subconjunto (~25-30%) alcança remissão durável com duração de 1-3 anos. AloHCT geralmente fora da tabela para este grupo, embora CR1 → aloHTC de intensidade reduzida condicionada é ocasionalmente perseguido em casos limítrofes. STUB — requer sinal de co-lead clinico.

CR + CRh rate 35% (95% CI 27-43); among CR + CRh responders, median DoR 25.9 mo, median time to CR + CRh 1.9 mo, 56-day mortality 8%. Transfusion independence achieved in 56% of baseline-dependent patients. FDA accelerated approval Dec 2022. Mechanistically: olutasidenib is a more selective mutant-IDH1 inhibitor than ivosidenib (in vitro selectivity for mIDH1 R132 variants over WT-IDH1 / IDH2). Differentiation syndrome incidence ~14% (similar to ivosidenib); hepatotoxicity boxed warning is distinguishing feature vs ivosidenib (no boxed warning). QTc prolongation less frequent than ivosidenib in cross-trial. STUB pending Clinical Co-Lead sign-off. Substituted benzamide that antagonizes d: Benzamida substituída que antagoniza os receptores dopaminérgicos D2 centralmente na zona de desencadeamento do quimiorreceptor (área pós-rema) e periféricamente no trato GI superior, reduzindo náuseas e acelerando o esvaziamento gástrico. Também um agonista dos receptores 5-HT4 (liberação potencial de acetilcolina no plexo entérico → peristalse aumentada) e, em doses elevadas (≥1 mg/kg), um antagonista 5-HT3 fraco. A ação proquinética distingue-a dos antagonistas puros do D2 e é terapêuticamente útil para gastroparesia induzida por quimioterapia, esvaziamento gástrico tardio induzido por opioides e dispepsia pós-tratamento. Aprovada pela FDA em 1979 para náuseas/vómitos e gastroparese; amplamente utilizada como antiemético de avanço em regimes de VNI. Razão de prevenção do câncer: ODC é um alvo c-Myc; as poliamina PACES (Fase III, Meyskens et al.): eflornitina 500 mg + sulidac 150 mg PO diários reduziu adenomas metacrônicos em ~70% ao longo de 36 meses em doentes com adenômes esporádicos prévios do cólon (Cancer Prev Res 2008); seguimento contínuo. Aprovado pela FDA (Iwilfin, 2024) para a terapêutica de manutenção de neuroblastoma de alto risco — primeira indicação oncológica para o agente.
Sulfoxide prodrug reduced by gut microbi: Sulfoxide prodrug reduced by gut microbiota and hepatic enzymes to active sulindac sulfide, which non-selectively inhibits COX-1 and COX-2, suppressing prostaglandin (especially PGE2) synthesis. Cancer- prevention rationale: COX-2 is upregulated in FAP adenomas; sulindac reduces polyp number and size in FAP (Giardiello NEJM 1993 RCT — 150 mg BID for 9 months, ~56% reduction in polyp number, ~65% in size; pooled trials in retained rectum post-colectomy show similar effect). PACES RCT (Meyskens 2008) combined eflornithine + sulindac reduced sporadic colorectal adenoma recurrence by ~70%. NOT FDA- labeled for chemoprevention; used off-label per NCCN Genetic Familial Colorectal 2025 in selected FAP patients (e.g., retained rectum, duodenal disease) under specialist hereditary-CRC team supervision.

Switch native E. coli → Erwinia or pegas: Switch native E. coli → Erwinia or pegaspargase after grade ≥2 hypersensitivity (no antigenic cross-reactivity between E. coli and Erwinia). Monitor lipase + amylase + glucose + fibrinogen + PT/aPTT + transaminases before each dose; hold for clinical pancreatitis. SMILE for NK/T-nasal lymphoma is the reference regimen (Yamaguchi 2008/2011) with ~80% ORR in newly-diagnosed advanced disease. Antithrombin III replacement when ATIII <60% is institutional; fibrinogen replacement (cryo or fibrinogen concentrate) when <100 mg/dL with active bleeding. Avoid prophylactic FFP — does not reduce thrombosis. Silent inactivation: monitor asparaginase activity level (target trough >0.1 IU/mL at day 7-14 post-dose) where lab access exists; switch preparations if subtherapeutic.

Synthetic imidazoquinoline TLR7 agonist. Binds TLR7 on plasmacytoid dendritic cells and monocytes/macrophages, triggering NF-κB-mediated release of IFN-α, TNF-α, and other pro-inflammatory cytokines. Induces a local Th1-skewed innate + cell-mediated immune response against virally-infected or dysplastic epithelium; not directly cytotoxic or antiviral itself. Used topically for HPV-associated and field- cancerization lesions (external genital warts, actinic keratosis, superficial BCC) where local immune-mediated clearance is desired.
Synthetic monocyclic β-lactam antibiotic: Synthetic monocyclic β-lactam antibiotic that binds penicillin- binding protein 3 (PBP-3) of aerobic Gram-negative bacilli with high affinity, inhibiting cell-wall synthesis and producing bactericidal effect. Activity narrowly restricted to aerobic Gram-negative bacteria including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Enterobacterales (most), Haemophilus, Neisseria. NO activity against Gram-positive bacteria, anaerobes, atypicals. Unique monobactam structure does NOT cross-react with penicillin or cephalosporin antibodies in IgE-mediated hypersensitivity, making aztreonam the preferred Gram-negative β-lactam for patients with documented severe penicillin allergy (including anaphylaxis). The exception is ceftazidime, which shares the aminothiazolyl side chain — patients with confirmed ceftazidime hypersensitivity may also react to aztreonam. FDA-approved 1986.

Synthetic prostaglandin E1 analog with g: Synthetic prostaglandin E1 analog with gastric mucosal protective effects (mucus + bicarbonate secretion, decreased gastric acid via enterochromaffin-like cell inhibition) and uterotonic activity. In oncology / cancer-prevention context: investigated as endometrial protection in tamoxifen users (theoretical rationale — endometrial PGE pathways). Evidence base is limited and inconsistent; not guideline-recommended for routine tamoxifen-associated endometrial protection. Primary FDA indications are NSAID-induced peptic ulcer prophylaxis and (off-label) obstetric uses.
Synthetic taurine analog with mixed acti: Synthetic taurine analog with mixed action on NMDA glutamate receptors (modulator) and GABAergic neurotransmission. Restores glutamatergic excitatory / GABAergic inhibitory balance disrupted by chronic alcohol use. Used to maintain abstinence in alcohol use disorder (AUD) after successful detoxification. First-line FDA-approved AUD pharmacotherapy alongside naltrexone and disulfiram. No effect on intoxication or withdrawal — purely abstinence maintenance.
Synthetic tetrahydroisoquinoline alkaloi: Synthetic tetrahydroisoquinoline alkaloid that binds the minor groove of DNA and stalls RNA polymerase II elongation, triggering RNAPII ubiquitination, double-strand breaks, and apoptosis selectively in transcription-addicted tumor cells. Also depletes tumor-associated macrophages. ATLANTIS (Phase III lurbinectedin + doxorubicin vs topotecan/CAV in 2L SCLC) failed its OS primary endpoint, but the pivotal single-arm Phase II Basket Study (NCT02454972, lurbinectedin monotherapy 3.2 mg/m² q21d) showed ORR 35% in 2L SCLC (CTFI ≥90 d ORR 45%; CTFI <90 d ORR 22%), supporting accelerated FDA approval Jun 2020.

T-ALL/T-LBL anterior mediastinal mass is: T-ALL/T-LBL anterior mediastinal mass is class-defining (~50-60% of T-ALL). Airway compromise + SVC syndrome are joint emergency presentations requiring HOLD on definitive induction — needs urgent steroids (prednisone or dexamethasone) to debulk, head-elevation, avoid supine GA. Per NCCN-BCELL ALL/LBL section: emergent steroid pre-phase before formal induction in symptomatic mediastinal mass. Per CALGB-10403: pediatric-inspired regimens begin with steroid pre-phase that addresses this. Direction HOLD because definitive induction is deferred until airway / SVC stabilized; priority 8 to win conflicts with TLS-emergency (which fires on the same patient). STUB — requires clinical co-lead signoff. Wiring suggestion: ALGO-T-ALL-1L step that branches on this RF to a steroid-pre-phase pathway before regimen selection.

TERT (Telomerase Reverse Transcriptase): TERT (Telomerase Reverse Transcriptase) is the catalytic subunit of telomerase. TERT promoter mutations (C228T or C250T, by chr5 coordinates) create de novo ETS family transcription factor binding sites, increasing TERT transcription and telomerase activity, extending cellular lifespan and enabling replicative immortality. Key clinical contexts: (1) Papillary thyroid cancer (PTC): TERT promoter mutations (~10–15% of PTC) are adverse prognostic markers, particularly when co-occurring with BRAF V600E (~8–12% of PTC). BRAF V600E + TERT promoter → mortality risk ~40× vs wild-type (Xing et al. NEJM 2014); this combination stratifies high-risk PTC requiring aggressive RAI and surveillance. (2) Follicular thyroid cancer: TERT mutations in ~15–20%. (3) GBM: TERT promoter mutations in ~70–80% (often co-occurring with EGFR amplification or IDH wild-type — defines molecular IDH-wild-type GBM). TERT mutation in IDH-wild-type astrocytoma with EGFR amplification or +7/-10 → WHO grade 4 GBM (CNS WHO 2021). TERT promoter mutations are central to WHO CNS tumor classification (2021 5th edition): (1) GBM (IDH-wildtype, WHO grade 4): TERT promoter mutation is one of three molecular defining features (together with EGFR amplification and chromosome +7/-10 copy number changes). An IDH-wildtype diffuse astrocytoma with any of these features meets criteria for molecular GBM diagnosis regardless of histologic grade. TERT alone: ~70–80% of GBM. TERT mutation identifies the most aggressive tumor biology within IDH-wildtype astrocytomas. No TERT-directed therapy available. (2) Oligodendroglioma (IDH-mutant, 1p/19q co-deleted): TERT promoter mutation is present in ~70% and is part of the canonical molecular definition. TERT testing is used to confirm oligodendroglioma classification (IDH + 1p/19q + TERT triple positive). (3) IDH-mutant astrocytoma (grade 2–4): TERT promoter mutation is less common (~20%) and associated with worse prognosis within IDH-mutant tumors; CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion is the main grade 4 determinant in IDH-mutant astrocytoma. Standard treatment for GBM is unchanged by TERT status: Stupp protocol (RT + temozolomide, followed by temozolomide maintenance). MGMT promoter methylation — not TERT — determines temozolomide sensitivity. ESCAT IIB: TERT is a diagnostic molecular classifier in glioma with strong prognostic significance but no actionable therapeutic target.

TGCT is classified as locally aggressive: TGCT is classified as locally aggressive (diffuse-type) or benign (localized). Despite benign histology, diffuse-type TGCT (formerly PVNS) causes severe joint destruction, pain, and functional disability, with high surgical recurrence rates (25–50%). Pexidartinib (CSF1R inhibitor) is the only FDA-approved systemic therapy (2019, ILLUMINATE trial): ORR 38%, durable response in responders, but significant hepatotoxicity risk (REMS program; transaminase monitoring mandatory). Surgery remains the primary modality; pexidartinib is reserved for patients with severe morbidity not amenable to surgery improvement. Malignant TGCT (9252/3) is extremely rare.
THOR (Loriot NEJM 2023) phase 3, cohort: THOR (Loriot NEJM 2023), fase 3, coorte 1: erdafitinib 8 mg PO diária (com titração a 9 mg se fosfato < 5,5 mg/dL dia 14) vs quimioterapia a escolha do investigador (docetaxel OR vinflunina) em carcinoma urotelial metastático com alterações selecionadas do FGFR2/3 (mutação S249C / R248C / G370C / Y373C fusão do FgFR2/3), após ≥1 linha anterior incluindo PD-(L)1 inibidor (n=266; 136 erdas vs 130 quimiologia). O objetivo primário foi o mOS 12,1 vs 7,8 mo (HR 0,64, p=0,005), o mPFS 5,6 vs 2,7 mo (RR 0,58), ORR 35,3% vs 8,5%. THOR coorte 2 (erda vs pembrolizumab em PD-(L)1-naive) foi negativo e não utilizado para apoiar a rotulagem. FDA convertida acelerada para aprovação completa Jan 2024 com base na THOr coorter 1. Toxicidade de classe: hiperfosfatemia (~76%), toxicidade ungueal (~57%), estomatite, retinopatia sérosa central (~25%, geralmente reversível). Fonte do ensaio SRC-THOR-LORIOT-2023 ainda não foi escrito em KB; citado por NCCN-BLADDER-2025 (diretriz urotelial ESMO ainda não publicada em KO também — marcada em corpo de commit).

TMPRSS2-ERG fusion detected on tumor RNA: TMPRSS2-ERG fusion detected on tumor RNA / FISH / IHC for ERG in localized or metastatic prostate cancer — INFORMATIONAL prognostic signal. Most common recurrent gene fusion in prostate cancer (~40-50% of localized PCa, ~15-30% of mCRPC). Conflicting prognostic literature: some series report worse PSA-relapse-free survival post-prostatectomy, others report no independent prognostic value after adjusting for Gleason / PSA / stage. NO predictive role established for ARSI, PARPi, taxane, or radioligand selection — does NOT modify treatment algorithm. Surfaces in MDT brief as: (1) molecular subtyping context, (2) potential clinical-trial enrollment criterion (ERG-positive cohorts in some experimental studies), (3) helpful for confirming prostate origin in metastatic-of-unknown-primary workup (TMPRSS2-ERG is highly prostate-specific).

TMPRSS2-ERG is the most common gene fusi: TMPRSS2-ERG is the most common gene fusion in prostate cancer (~50% of Caucasian prostate adenocarcinomas, ~20-30% in Asian and African-American populations — frequency varies by ancestry). Mechanism: androgen-responsive TMPRSS2 promoter drives aberrant ERG expression after interstitial 21q22 deletion (~2/3 of cases) or translocation. Clinical relevance: PROGNOSTIC, not Tx-modifying. Original Tomlins 2005 (Science) report linked fusion to aggressive disease; subsequent meta-analyses (e.g., Pettersson 2012, Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev) showed prognostic signal weaker than initially claimed and confounded by Gleason / stage. PARPi-sensitivity hypothesis (ETS-fusions causing replicative stress → PARPi response) TESTED but not validated as a monotherapy biomarker — ERG status alone does NOT qualify for olaparib / niraparib / talazoparib (which require HRR mutations). Use in KB: ships as biomarker only — no IND, no algorithm step. May be used in MDT brief to confirm prostate- origin in challenging metastasis-of-unknown-primary cases (ERG-IHC in metastasis = strong prostate-origin signal). T-DXd (trastuzumab-deruxtecan) preferred 2L+ for HER2+ post-trastuzumab failure (DESTINY-Gastric01).
TOPAZ-1 (Oh DY et al., NEJM Evid 2022;1(: TOPAZ-1 (Oh DY et al., NEJM Evid 2022;1(8):EVIDoa2200015; NCT03875235): durvalumab 1500 mg q3w + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² + cisplatin 25 mg/m² (D1, D8 q3w x up to 8 cycles), then durvalumab 1500 mg q4w maintenance, vs placebo + gem-cis in 1L advanced BTC (n=685). Primary endpoint OS: mOS 12.8 vs 11.5 mo (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.66-0.97, p=0.021); mPFS 7.2 vs 5.7 mo (HR 0.75); ORR 26.7% vs 18.7%. Benefit consistent across PD-L1 CPS subgroups and BTC anatomic subsites (intra-/extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder cancer). FDA-approved Sep 2022 for 1L advanced BTC. NCCN category 1 preferred regimen. Cisplatin (D1/D8 schedule, not standard D1-only) is per protocol — total cycles capped at 8 for chemo backbone; durvalumab maintenance continues until progression / toxicity. STUB pending Clinical Co-Lead sign-off per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode exemption.

TPS-50% bypass of chemo applies only AFT: O TPS-50% de bypass da quimio se aplica apenas APÓS todas as mutações do motorista são excluídas (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF V600E, MET ex14, RET, NTRK, KRAS G12C, HER2 — no mínimo o painel SOC). A doença EGFR-mutante ou rearanjada com ALK responde POORly à IC, mesmo em TPS-100% — a direcção do motoristas TKI é sempre a 1L correta. TPS 1-49% — quimio + IC combo (KEYNOTE-189 não escamoso, KEYNOSTE-407 escamosa) preferido; pembrolizumab em monoterapia ainda é uma opção (KeyNOTE-042) mas inferior a combo. TPS < 1% — quimio + IC combo ou quimio+ipi/nivo (CheckMate-9LA); monoterapia não recomendada. A co-mutação STK11/KEAP1 é um preditor negativo para a resposta ICI mesmo em alta TPS — biomarcador emergente para quimiocombo + IC sobre monoterapia. Detecção: 22C3 laboratório central IHC preferido; SP263 (utilizado em estudos IMPower) e 22C3, não são intercambiáveis para o corte de 50% (comparação de impressão azul). As metástases cerebrais não são uma contraindicação se assintomáticas e ≤2 cm — KEYNOTE-024 incluiu mets cerebro controlado.

TROP2 expression in NSCLC — datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) is a TROP2-directed deruxtecan antibody-drug conjugate. TROPION-Lung01 (Ahn 2023) phase-3 randomized previously-treated metastatic NSCLC to Dato-DXd vs docetaxel (mPFS 4.4 vs 3.7 mo, HR 0.75; benefit concentrated in non-squamous subgroup mPFS 5.6 vs 3.7 mo, HR 0.63). TROP2 is broadly expressed across NSCLC histologies (IHC enrollment not required) — TROP2 IHC is informational, not gating. Candidate RF positions Dato-DXd in 2L+ non-squamous NSCLC as a non-platinum cytotoxic alternative to docetaxel.

TROPION-Breast01 (NCT05104866): Phase II: TROPION-Breast01 (NCT05104866): Phase III, HR+/HER2- metastatic breast post-ET + 1-2 prior chemo lines. Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) 6 mg/kg q3w vs investigator-choice chemo (eribulin / vinorelbine / gemcitabine / capecitabine). Median PFS 6.9 vs 4.9 mo (HR 0.63). FDA approval Jan 2025 (Datroway). Distinguishing AE profile vs T-DXd: higher stomatitis + ocular toxicity, lower (~3% vs ~12%) ILD rate. TROP2-IHC not required as predictive biomarker per current label (broad-eligibility design). When HER2-low IHC 1+ / 2+ ISH- coexists, T-DXd (DESTINY-Breast04 PFS 10.1 vs 5.4 mo, HR 0.51) is preferred over Dato-DXd by efficacy margin; Dato-DXd is the option for IHC-0 (HER2-zero) patients ineligible for T-DXd. Bibliographic record SRC-TROPION-BREAST01-BARDIA-2024 is available; clinical claim linkage requires dual clinical sign-off. UA access: not registered; named-patient import / EAP only.

TSC1 (hamartin) forms a heterodimeric co: TSC1 (hamartin) forms a heterodimeric complex with TSC2 (tuberin) that acts as a GTPase activating protein (GAP) for Rheb, maintaining mTORC1 in an inactive state. Loss of either TSC1 or TSC2 → constitutive mTORC1 activation → protein synthesis, cell growth, proliferation. Clinical manifestations of TSC1 loss: (1) Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) — germline TSC1 (~30%) or TSC2 (~70%): cortical tubers, SEGA, renal AML, cardiac rhabdomyomas, LAM (females), skin lesions. TSC1 germline associated with milder phenotype than TSC2. (2) LAM — predominantly somatic TSC2 (>80%) or rarely TSC1 in sporadic LAM. TSC-associated LAM has germline TSC mutation. (3) Renal angiomyolipoma (sporadic) — somatic TSC1/TSC2 in ~50%. mTOR inhibitors (everolimus, sirolimus) are approved for multiple TSC/LAM manifestations: - Sirolimus: LAM (MILES 2011; FDA 2015) - Everolimus: SEGA (EXIST-1), renal AML (EXIST-2), TSC-related seizures (EXIST-3); renal cell carcinoma (SRC-BOLERO2-BASELGA-2012 — different indication via PIK3/AKT/mTOR pathway). Note: the BIO entity covers TSC1 specifically; TSC2 mutations are clinically similar but a separate gene — both treated with mTOR inhibitors.

TSC1 germline pathogenic variants drive Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) — an mTOR-pathway hyperactivation syndrome with multi-organ tumor predisposition: subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA), renal angiomyolipomas (AML), lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM, females), cardiac rhabdomyomas, and cortical tubers. Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (per Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Consensus Conference / NCCN CNS): brain MRI q1-3y through age 25 for SEGA, renal MRI/US q1-3y from diagnosis (lifelong) for AML, pulmonary function tests + HRCT chest q5-10y in adult females for LAM, baseline echocardiogram + ECG, dermatology and ophthalmology exam annually. mTOR inhibitors (everolimus, sirolimus) are active across SEGA, growing renal AMLs (≥3 cm), and LAM — these are surveillance-triggered interventions, not prophylactic. ESCAT IIA (predisposition with established surveillance + targeted therapy on progression).

TSC2 germline pathogenic variants drive Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) — the more clinically severe of the two TSC genotypes (TSC2 carriers have earlier onset and broader phenotype than TSC1). Same multi-organ tumor spectrum as TSC1: SEGA, renal AML (typically more numerous and earlier in TSC2), LAM, cardiac rhabdomyoma, cortical tubers. Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol identical to TSC1 (per TSC Consensus Conference 2012 + 2021 update / NCCN CNS): brain MRI q1-3y through age 25 for SEGA, renal MRI/US q1-3y lifelong, PFT + HRCT chest q5-10y in adult females, baseline echocardiogram, annual dermatology + ophthalmology exam. Contiguous-gene TSC2/PKD1 deletions present with severe polycystic kidney disease in addition to AML and require nephrology co-management. mTOR inhibitors (everolimus, sirolimus) active across SEGA, renal AML ≥3 cm, and LAM. ESCAT IIA.
TSC2 germline — drives Tuberous Sclerosi: TSC2 germline — impulsiona o Complexo da Esclerose Tuberosa (TSC); tipicamente mais grave fenótipo do que TSC1. O mesmo espectro tumoral: SEGA, AML renal, LAM, rabdomismos cardíacos, tubérculos corticais + achados cutâneos (angiofibromas, shagreen patch). inibidores do mTOR (everolimus, sirolimus) ativos. Deleção de genes contíguos PKD1 em alguns portadores → doença renal poliquística de início precoce. STUB pendente de sinalização de dois-Co-Lead.

Tazemetostat (EPZ-6438), um inibidor da metiltransferase EZH2, é aprovado pela FDA (janeiro de 2020) para adultos e pacientes pediátricos (≥16 anos) com sarcoma epitelóide metastático ou localmente avançado não elegível para ressecção completa. Esta foi a primeira aprovação pela Fda nesta doença e a primeira autorização visada pela EZh2 em tumores sólidos. EZ H-202 fase II (Gounder et al., Lancet Oncology 2020): N=62 avaliável; objetivo primário ORR pelo RECIST 1.1. ORR: 15% (9/62; 1 CR, 8 PR); taxa de benefício clínico (CR+PR+SD ≥32 semanas): 26%. mDOR em respondentes: não atingido no momento da análise. Taxa de controle da doença: ~26% com DP durável. Perfil de segurança: geralmente bem tolerado; risco raro de linfoma de células T secundária (inibidor da classe EZH2); risco de malignidade mielóide com uso a longo prazo (monitorização recomendada). Perda do INI1 (IHC) é o diagnóstico de companhia — necessário para o diagnóstico e elegibilidade. A quimioterapia padrão (com base em doxorrubicina) continua a ser uma opção para doentes adequados com doença de rápido progresso; o tazemetostato preferido para o curso de crescimento lento/indolente.

Y537S confers more aggressive biology than D538G in some series. ESR1-WT post-AI patients did not benefit from elacestrant in EMERALD — fulvestrant + capivasertib / alpelisib alternative. Testicular GCT is the most common solid: O TCG testicular é o tumor sólido mais comum em homens com 15-35 anos e um dos cânceres mais curados mesmo em fase metastática (curas de quimioterapia baseadas em BEP ~80-92% de TCG de bom/risco intermedio metastático; ~50% de baixo risco). O diagnóstico precoce por meio do auto-exame + ultrassonografia é crítico.Todo o estadiamento requer soro AFP, beta-hCG, LDH no diagnóstico e pós-orquiectomia para determinar a trajetória dos marcadores. O RPLND (dissecção de linfonodos retroperitoneais) é utilizado para: massas residuais após quimioterapia (seminoma → guiado por PET; NSGCT → cirurgia para >1cm residual), estágio patológico I vigilância-alternativa NSGTC.
Testicular GCT is unique — curative even: Testicular GCT is unique — curative even at metastatic stage for most patients. Post-BEP residual mass management: seminoma >3cm → PET-guided (FDG-avid → biopsy/resection; FDG-negative → observe); NSGCT >1cm → RPLND for residual teratoma resection. Surveillance after good-risk GCT: CT CAP q3-4 months year 1, then q6 months year 2-3; markers q1-2 months year 1. 2L salvage: TIP (paclitaxel + ifosfamide + cisplatin) or VIP (vinblastine + ifosfamide + cisplatin) for cisplatin-sensitive relapse; high-dose chemotherapy + ASCT at specialized centers for multiply relapsed/refractory GCT.

Tetracycline binds reversibly to the 30S: Tetracycline binds reversibly to the 30S ribosomal subunit at the A site, preventing aminoacyl-tRNA from associating with the ribosome and blocking the elongation step of bacterial protein synthesis. Broad spectrum: Gram-positives, Gram-negatives, atypicals (Mycoplasma, Chlamydia, Rickettsia), spirochetes, Helicobacter pylori (including metronidazole- and clarithromycin-resistant strains in PBMT quadruple therapy). The vast majority of BCCs are cured with: The vast majority of BCCs are cured with surgery or radiation. Hedgehog inhibitors (vismodegib, sonidegib) are approved only for locally advanced unresectable or metastatic BCC — a small fraction of all BCCs. Gorlin syndrome (PTCH1 germline) warrants genetic counseling and lifelong surveillance. SMO inhibitors cause significant side effects (muscle cramps, alopecia, dysgeusia, weight loss) limiting long-term use. Cemiplimab (anti-PD-1) is FDA-approved for locally advanced/metastatic BCC after HHI failure.

Therapeutic radioiodine (I-131) exposure for differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) ablation/treatment OR Graves' disease — cumulative doses ≥100 mCi (3.7 GBq) lifetime confer small-but-real increased risk of secondary malignancies. Strongest signal: leukemia (RR ~1.5-2.0 above population baseline; latency 2-10 years), salivary gland cancer (RR ~1.3-2.0; latency 5-15 years), breast cancer in females (RR ~1.2-1.4; lower-quality evidence, dose-dependent), bladder cancer (modest signal). Iodine concentrates in salivary glands + stomach + bladder during excretion; non-target dose drives secondary cancer signal. Risk modestly higher at younger ages of exposure (proliferating tissues more radiosensitive). Prevention- persona RedFlag (§20, v0.3 iatrogenic expansion).

Thienobenzodiazepine atypical antipsycho: Thienobenzodiazepine atypical antipsychotic with high-affinity antagonism at multiple receptors implicated in nausea and vomiting: dopamine D2 (mesolimbic), serotonin 5-HT2A/2C, histamine H1, muscarinic M1, and α1-adrenergic. Multi-receptor blockade in the vomiting center, area postrema, and chemoreceptor trigger zone produces broad-spectrum antiemetic effect across acute, delayed, and breakthrough CINV phases. Adding olanzapine 10 mg PO days 1-4 to triple antiemetic prophylaxis (NK1 + 5-HT3 + dex) improves complete-response rate by ~10% absolute for HEC (Navari, NEJM 2016). Particularly effective for refractory or breakthrough nausea where single-receptor antagonists have failed. Approved by FDA September 1996 (psychiatric indications); CINV use is guideline-supported off-label / on-label depending on jurisdiction.

Third of three Ashkenazi Jewish founder: Third of three Ashkenazi Jewish founder mutations (combined carrier frequency ~2.5% in AJ; ~1.5% for this BRCA2 variant alone in some cohorts). Single-T deletion in exon 11 causing frameshift and premature termination in the DNA-binding domain region — abolishes RAD51-mediated homologous-recombination repair. Modern HGVS notation c.5946delT; legacy notation 6174delT (older mRNA-numbering convention). Lifetime cancer risks consistent with BRCA2 average: breast ~50-60%, ovarian ~15-20%, male breast ~6-8%, pancreas ~5-7%, prostate ~20-25%. Higher pancreas risk than BRCA1 — CAPS-Consortium pancreatic surveillance (annual MRI/MRCP or EUS from age 50 or 10 years before youngest PDAC in family) applies to BRCA2 carriers with PDAC family history. Same breast/ovarian surveillance and risk-reduction protocols as other BRCA2 pathogenic variants (annual MRI from 25-30, RRSO 40-45). NCCN 2025 endorses population-wide AJ founder-panel testing. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff.

Resectable: surgery + adjuvant capecitabine 6 months (BILCAP). Liver transplant for selected pCCA after Mayo neoadjuvant protocol (chemo-radiation + brachy → exam-under-anesthesia → transplant). Advanced 1L: gemcitabine + cisplatin + durvalumab (TOPAZ-1) replaced gem-cis monotherapy as standard. Pembrolizumab + gem-cis is an alternative (KEYNOTE-966). Advanced 2L+ by genotype (intrahepatic CCA enrichment): - FGFR2 fusion / rearrangement (~10–20% iCCA): pemigatinib (FIGHT-202) or futibatinib (FOENIX-CCA2) — both FDA-approved. Hyperphosphatemia is on-target effect. - IDH1 R132 (~15% iCCA): ivosidenib (ClarIDHy) — modest PFS benefit. - HER2 IHC 3+ / amplified (~5–10% perihilar/distal): trastuzumab + pertuzumab (MyPathway) or trastuzumab deruxtecan (DESTINY-PanTumor02); zanidatamab (HERIZON-BTC-01). - BRAF V600E (~5%): dabrafenib + trametinib (ROAR — tumor-agnostic). - MSI-H / dMMR (~2–3%): pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-158). - NTRK fusion (rare): larotrectinib / entrectinib. Three subsites with distinct biology and: Three subsites with distinct biology and treatment patterns. Early glottic (T1-T2N0): radiation OR transoral laser microsurgery (TLM) — both ~90% local control with voice preservation as key endpoint. Locally advanced: larynx-preservation chemoradiation (cisplatin + RT) per RTOG 91-11 / VA-trial paradigm vs total laryngectomy + postoperative RT — patient preference / fitness drives choice. Recurrent / metastatic: pembrolizumab ± chemo per KEYNOTE-048 (same framework as broader HNSCC). Smoking cessation surveillance dominates prevention narrative.

Thymidine analog; intracellularly phosph: Analógico da timidina; fosforilado intracelularmente pela timididina quinase/timidilato quinasa/difosfato quinaso nucleosídeo a trifosfato ZDV, que compete com o dTTP para a transcriptase reversa VIH-1/HTLV-1 e atua como um terminador de cadeia obrigatório (falta de 3'-OH para maior alongamento). Na leucemia / linfoma de células T adultos (ATLL) impulsionada por HTLV-1, a AZT combinada com IFN-α exerce actividade antineoplásica não apenas atribuível à inibição da transcriptase reversa: induz a apoptose via supressão da via NF-κB, reduz a regulação da unidade de ciclo celular HTV-1 mediada pelos impostos, e se sinergiza com a sinalização anti proliferativa do interferão tipo I (meta-análise de Bazarbachi 2010: ~50% de RC durável em ATLL indolente).
Thyroglobulin doubling time <12 months i: Thyroglobulin doubling time <12 months is a validated adverse prognostic marker (Miyauchi et al, JCEM 2011) — predicts shorter OS in DTC. RAI refractoriness defined per ATA criteria (Schlumberger consensus): no uptake at diagnosis, lesion-level uptake but no response, or progression after RAI ≥600 mCi cumulative. Lenvatinib is 1L for RAI-refractory progressive PTC (SELECT trial); cabozantinib COSMIC-311 is FDA-approved 2L post-lenvatinib (PFS 11 vs 1.9 mo placebo). DTC→ATC dedifferentiation: re-biopsy any new rapidly enlarging mass (especially neck) — disease tempo changes dramatically. Brain metastases rare in PTC; if present, consider stereotactic RT + CNS-penetrant TKI. Selpercatinib for RET-fusion / pralsetinib for RET-fusion pediatric / adolescent.

Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC): estrogen receptor (ER) <1% nuclear staining on IHC AND progesterone receptor (PR) <1% nuclear staining on IHC AND HER2-negative (IHC 0 or 1+, OR IHC 2+ with ISH non-amplified). TNBC represents ~15-20% of all invasive breast cancers and is defined by the absence of all three hormone/growth-factor receptor targets. Clinical significance: TNBC lacks ER, PR, and HER2 targets, precluding endocrine therapy (tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors) and HER2-directed therapy. Treatment is chemotherapy-based: - Early TNBC: pembrolizumab + neoadjuvant chemotherapy (KEYNOTE-522; Schmid NEJM 2022) — pCR rate 64.8% vs 51.2% with chemo alone, regardless of PD-L1 status. KEYNOTE-522 is the standard-of-care regimen. - Metastatic TNBC (BRCA-WT): pembrolizumab + chemotherapy (KEYNOTE-355) for CPS ≥10; chemotherapy alone (nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel, or gemcitabine+carboplatin...

Two biological subgroups (HPV-driven vs: Two biological subgroups (HPV-driven vs HPV-independent) managed similarly anatomically. Treatment: early-stage (Tis, Ta, T1a) — organ-sparing approaches (topical 5-FU / imiquimod for Tis; CO2- laser or wide local excision for T1a; glansectomy for selected T2); advanced primary (T2-T4) — partial / total penectomy; inguinal nodal management — dynamic sentinel node biopsy or modified inguinal lymphadenectomy per cN0 vs cN+ status (highly morbid, complications common); metastatic — cisplatin + 5-FU OR TIP (paclitaxel + ifosfamide + cisplatin) per EAU; pembrolizumab in MSI-H subset. HPV vaccination of boys (Gardasil-9) is the primary prevention modality alongside neonatal circumcision discussion.
Two biological subgroups managed similar: Two biological subgroups managed similarly anatomically but with distinct prevention implications: HPV-driven (vaccination prevents precursor lesions; screening with vulvar exam + biopsy of any persistent lesion) vs HPV-independent (lichen sclerosus surveillance is the dominant prevention modality; topical clobetasol may reduce malignant transformation in select cohorts). Treatment: early-stage — wide local excision ± inguinal sentinel node biopsy (GROINSS-V paradigm replacing routine complete inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy); locally advanced — definitive chemoradiation (cisplatin + RT); metastatic — pembrolizumab if PD-L1+ (KEYNOTE-158 cohort). Vaginal SCC managed similarly with RT-based approaches (anatomic constraints limit surgical options).

Two major treatment philosophies: COG (N: Two major treatment philosophies: COG (North American) — upfront surgery + adjuvant chemo (± RT) based on stage + histology. SIOP (European) — pre-operative chemo (4-6 weeks) → surgery → adjuvant based on response + histology. Both achieve >90% OS in favorable- histology disease. Chemotherapy backbone: vincristine + actinomycin ± doxorubicin per stage / histology / risk group. Anaplastic histology requires intensified regimens (ifosfamide + carboplatin + etoposide). Cascade screening obligatory for syndromic carriers — abdominal US q3-4 months from birth to age 7 in Beckwith-Wiedemann / WAGR.

Umbrella disease; therapy is HISTOLOGY-d: Umbrella disease; therapy is HISTOLOGY-driven. Two histologies are highly actionable: - Mammary analogue secretory carcinoma (MASC, parotid most common): near-100% ETV6-NTRK3 fusion (or NTRK1/2 partner variants); larotrectinib / entrectinib transformative in advanced disease (FDA tumor-agnostic). - Salivary duct carcinoma (SDC): aggressive, often parotid; molecular profile mimics breast / prostate: * AR-positive (~70-80%): bicalutamide + LHRH agonist (EORTC-1206); active even without prior antiandrogen exposure. * HER2-amplified (~30-40%): trastuzumab + docetaxel (Takahashi et al, JCO 2019); trastuzumab deruxtecan in DESTINY-PanTumor02; zanidatamab. * HRAS mutant (~10-15%): tipifarnib (KO-TIP-007). * PIK3CA / PI3K pathway: alpelisib + tipifarnib in KURRENT-HN. - Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC): MYB-NFIB fusion ~60% (not currently drugged); NOTCH1 mutation ~15% (gamma-secretase inhibitors — AL101 / ACCURACY trial). Indolent course with late distant relapses (lung most common). Chemotherapy generally low-yield; multikinase TKIs (lenvatinib) modest activity. - Mucoepidermoid carcinoma: CRTC1-MAML2 fusion ~50% (prognostic, not therapeutic). Surgery + adjuvant RT for high-grade.

Universal B-cell receptor component — ex: Universal B-cell receptor component — expressed on virtually all mature B-cell neoplasms (DLBCL, FL, MCL, MZL, CLL, Burkitt, plasma cell neoplasms variably). Primarily relevant as therapeutic target for polatuzumab vedotin (anti-CD79b ADC; replaces vincristine in Pola-R-CHP for DLBCL). Routine confirmation not required for polatuzumab eligibility — assumed positive on B-cell histology — but documented when negative or weak as caveat for ADC efficacy.
Universal CD30+ in systemic ALCL. ~40-60: Universal CD30+ in systemic ALCL. ~40-60% PTCL NOS / AITL. Required for brentuximab vedotin-based regimens (CHP-Bv, A+AVD).
Universal adverse marker across most hem: Universal adverse marker across most hematologic + solid malignancies — predicts poor response to chemo + chemoimmuno; selects for novel- agent regimens / targeted therapies / cellular therapy / alloSCT. **Cross-disease decision impact in our KB (current scope):** - **CLL/SLL**: TP53-mut OR del(17p) → contraindicates chemoimmuno (FCR/BR); favors fixed-duration VenO (CLL14) over BTKi continuous in some guidelines. Captured in composite BIO-CLL-HIGH-RISK-GENETICS + RF-CLL-HIGH-RISK. - **MCL**: TP53-mut → predicts chemoimmuno failure (intensive R-CHOP/R-DHAP+autoSCT outcomes substantially worse); routes to BTKi-based 1L (acalabrutinib+R) regardless of fitness. Captured in RF-MCL-BLASTOID-OR-TP53. - **MM**: del(17p) part of high-risk cytogenetics composite — drives quadruplet (D-VRd) over triplet (VRd). Captured in BIO-MM-CYTOGENETICS-HR + RF-MM-HIGH-RISK-CYTOGENETICS. - **DLBCL** (future scope): predicts R-CHOP failure; flag for early CAR-T pathway consideration at 2L+. Not yet driving 1L algorithm. - **AML** (future scope, not in KB yet): TP53-mut AML has dismal chemo outcomes — currently routes directly to alloSCT consideration + venetoclax-azacitidine for unfit + clinical trials....
Universal at metastatic NSCLC diagnosis. Distinguishes ICI-monotherapy candidates from combination-therapy population.
Universal because geriatric-assessment n: Universal, porque as necessidades de avaliação geriátrica são impulsionadas pela pessoa e terapêutica proposta, não histologia tumoral. Trata-se de metadados somente de avaliação: um oncologista confirma a interpretação e qualquer adaptação terapêutica.
Universal because specialist pediatric c: Universal because specialist pediatric coordination is a care-setting requirement across childhood cancers. It surfaces a safety check only; the treating team confirms all diagnosis- and protocol-specific choices.
Universal fields for fitness assessment,: Universal fields for fitness assessment, infection status, and organ function. Fill in whatever is in the chart — empty fields are simply not evaluated by the engine (replaces 'unevaluated RedFlag' warnings).
Universal pathology-grading framework. W: Universal pathology-grading framework. WHO 2022 endorses ISUP grade group nomenclature; older Gleason notation still common in clinical reports.
Universal proliferation marker across he: Universal proliferation marker across hematologic + solid neoplasms: - **Burkitt** (~100% — defining): highest Ki-67 of any human malignancy - **HGBL** (~80-100%) - **DLBCL** (~60-80%): higher Ki-67 may identify "double-expressor" aggressive subset - **MCL** (~10-50% — defines MIPI-b): >30% = blastoid-like aggressive, triggers RF-MCL-BLASTOID-OR-TP53 → BTKi-R route - **FL** grade: 1-2 typically <30%; grade 3 ≥30% (informs grade) - **Indolent NHL** (CLL, MZL, indolent FL): typically <20% - **Plasma cell myeloma**: >40-60% may indicate plasma cell leukemia transformation Algorithm-impacting in MCL (drives BTKi-R via blastoid RedFlag at >30%). Informational/grading elsewhere.
Universal screening gap age 50+ · CRC +: Distância universal de rastreamento com idade 50+ · CRC + mamografia + captação de Pap

Venetoclax (BCL2 inhibitor) + azacitidine or decitabine is FDA-approved (Oct 2020) for newly diagnosed AML in patients ≥75 years or those ineligible for intensive induction chemotherapy, regardless of BCL2 expression status. However, BCL2 protein overexpression and specific co-mutations (IDH1/2, NPM1) are strong predictors of venetoclax response. VIALE-A trial (DiNardo et al. NEJM 2020 — venetoclax + azacitidine vs azacitidine): mOS 14.7 vs 9.6 mo (HR 0.66, p<0.001); CR/CRi rate 66.4% vs 28.3%. BCL2 IHC high-expressors had superior outcomes in retrospective VIALE-A subanalyses. Molecular co-mutation context: NPM1-mutated AML: CR ~75% with ven+aza; IDH2-mutated: CR ~67%; IDH1-mutated: CR ~57%; TP53-mutated: CR ~40% (inferior). AML with t(8;21) or inv(16) (CBF-AML): poor ven response — avoid ven+aza in favor of intensive 7+3 + GO when fit. ESCAT IIB reflects that BCL2 IHC alone is not a mandated companion diagnostic — clinical eligibility criteria (age/fitness) are the primary drivers; BCL2 overexpression adds predictive value in molecular context.

WM is overwhelmingly an elderly disease: WM is overwhelmingly an elderly disease (median age 70 at diagnosis). Frail elderly: BR with reduced bendamustine doses (70 mg/m² instead of 90) per StiL elderly subgroup; or rituximab monotherapy weekly x4 + maintenance for low-burden symptomatic disease. Continuous BTKi: zanubrutinib preferred over ibrutinib in elderly with cardiac comorbidity (ASPEN — lower AF, hypertension, sudden cardiac events). IgM flare with rituximab can precipitate hyperviscosity in elderly; pre-treat with plasmapheresis if baseline IgM >40 g/L. Avoid intensive Dex-R-Cyclo in very frail (cytopenias, infection risk).

WT1 germline pathogenic variants drive a spectrum of pediatric kidney predispositions: WAGR syndrome (11p13 contiguous-gene deletion — Wilms tumor, aniridia, genitourinary anomalies, range of intellectual disability; Wilms risk ~30-50%), Denys-Drash syndrome (missense in zinc- finger domain — pseudohermaphroditism + diffuse mesangial sclerosis + Wilms tumor; risk ~50-90%), and Frasier syndrome (intron-9 splice variants — 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis + focal segmental glomerulosclerosis; gonadoblastoma risk). Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (per International Society of Paediatric Oncology / SIOP-RTSG + COG Renal Tumor Committee Consensus / Kalish et al. 2017): renal ultrasound every 3 months from diagnosis through age 7-8 (Wilms incidence peaks before age 5 and falls steeply after age 7), urinalysis at each visit, blood pressure monitoring. Multi-disciplinary involvement: pediatric oncology + nephrology (renal function + proteinuria) + endocrinology (gonadal dysgenesis management) + genetics. Prophylactic gonadectomy is recommended in Frasier syndrome to prevent gonadoblastoma....
WT1 germline — drives WAGR (11p13 contig: WT1 germline — drives WAGR (11p13 contiguous-gene deletion: Wilms, aniridia, genitourinary anomalies, range of intellectual disability), Denys-Drash syndrome (pseudohermaphroditism + diffuse mesangial sclerosis + Wilms), and Frasier syndrome. Pediatric Wilms tumor risk ~50% in Denys-Drash, ~30-50% in WAGR. Surveillance: renal US every 3 months until age 7 in known carriers. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff.

WT1 mutations occur in ~10-15% of AML bu: WT1 mutations occur in ~10-15% of AML but are most clinically impactful when co-occurring with other adverse features. The dual role of WT1 (somatic mutation as prognostic marker + WT1 transcript overexpression as MRD marker) is unique among AML molecular markers. Per ELN 2022, WT1 mutations alone in NPM1-mutant, FLT3-ITD-negative AML do not confer adverse risk. Key clinical decision: WT1 mutation in AML with FLT3-ITD high allelic ratio → adverse risk → allogeneic HSCT in CR1 strongly recommended.

Well-differentiated or poorly-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor with Ki67 >20% (WHO 2019 G3). High-grade disease is clinically and therapeutically distinct from G1/G2: well-differentiated G3 pNET may still respond to everolimus/sunitinib/SSA but outcomes are inferior; poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC, Ki67 typically >55%) requires platinum- etoposide chemotherapy (CAPEOX/EP/IP). Engine flag routes to MDT review.
Well-differentiated pNET G1/G2 is the do: Well-differentiated pNET G1/G2 is the dominant subtype in clinical practice (non-functional, discovered incidentally or via abdominal mass/liver mets). Grading per WHO 2019: G1 Ki67 <3%, G2 Ki67 3–20%. G3 well-differentiated pNET (Ki67 >20%) occupies a grey zone — still well-differentiated morphologically but higher proliferation; NCCN recommends everolimus/sunitinib/SSA ± chemo; not modelled separately here (flagged via RF-NET-HIGH-GRADE-G3 for MDT review). Distinguishing from poorly differentiated NEC (ICD-O 8246/3) is essential: NEC requires platinum-etoposide chemotherapy (not SSA/TKI/mTOR). Key trials: RADIANT-3 (everolimus, Yao NEJM 2011), Raymond 2011 (sunitinib), CLARINET pNET subgroup (lanreotide). Surgery remains the only curative option for localized disease.

Wilson's disease (autosomal recessive ATP7B-mutated copper-transport disorder with hepatic and/or neuropsychiatric manifestations; Leipzig score ≥4 confirmatory) in an individual without a current HCC diagnosis. Historically considered a low-risk cirrhosis etiology for HCC, but contemporary cohorts (van Meer et al. Liver Int 2015; Pfeiffenberger et al. J Hepatol 2018) report HCC incidence of ~0.5-1%/year in cirrhotic Wilson's — exceeding the AASLD 1.5%/year surveillance-threshold in the cirrhotic subset. Risk concentrated in patients with established cirrhosis (especially decompensated disease) and those with prolonged uncontrolled copper accumulation. Adherent copper-chelation therapy (penicillamine, trientine, zinc) reduces hepatic copper burden but does not eliminate residual HCC risk in patients who already developed cirrhosis. Workhorse corticosteroid for: (1) acute: Workhorse corticosteroid for: (1) acute infusion reactions and anaphylaxis adjunct (40-125 mg IV after epinephrine); (2) immune- related adverse events from checkpoint inhibitors — the defining role; (3) CRS escalation when tocilizumab inadequate. Compared to hydrocortisone: more potent per mg (4-5×), longer duration, less mineralocorticoid effect (preferred when fluid retention undesirable). Compared to dexamethasone: slightly less potent (×6), shorter duration, but lower CNS penetration (slightly less psychiatric AE per equivalent dose); dex preferred for cerebral edema and antiemesis, methylprednisolone preferred for irAE management per NCCN / ESMO immunotherapy toxicity guidelines. CRITICAL: high-dose pulse (≥250 mg IV) must be infused over ≥30 min — rapid bolus risks fatal cardiac arrhythmia. Aprepitant DDI: aprepitant increases methylprednisolone exposure ~2.5× — reduce methylprednisolone ~50% when both prescribed (e.g., in HEC chemotherapy with antiemetic regimen). Single bolus of 40-125 mg has minimal long-term consequences; courses ≥2 weeks require taper to prevent adrenal crisis. Workhorse fluoroquinolone for Gram-negat: Workhorse fluoroquinolone for Gram-negative + Pseudomonas. In oncology, the principal use is IV-to-PO step-down therapy after documented Gram-negative bacteremia / UTI / intra-abdominal infection responding to initial broad-spectrum, allowing earlier discharge. ALSO used for outpatient management of low-risk febrile neutropenia (MASCC score ≥21, no comorbidities, expected ANC recovery <7 days) with the IDSA-recommended ciprofloxacin + amoxicillin-clavulanate oral regimen. NOT used for FN prophylaxis — that role belongs to levofloxacin, which has better Gram-positive coverage (esp. viridans streptococci, a major mucositis-related bacteremia source). Class-wide FDA / EMA 2018 warning restricts fluoroquinolones to serious infections without alternatives — applies to ciprofloxacin. Polyvalent cation chelation is the most common cause of treatment failure with oral therapy — patient counselling critical. CYP1A2 inhibition causes major DDIs (tizanidine contraindicated; theophylline doubles). Ukraine: cheap, ubiquitous, NSZU-covered.

del(5q) is detected in ~10-15% of MDS-LR: del(5q) is detected in ~10-15% of MDS-LR cases. WHO 5th edition recognizes "MDS with isolated del(5q)" as a distinct entity defined by the 5q deletion as the sole cytogenetic abnormality (or with one additional non-monosomy-7 abnormality), <5% BM blasts, and characteristic clinical features (macrocytic anemia, normal-to-high platelets, hypolobated megakaryocytes). Lenalidomide MDS-003 (Houston phase-2) + MDS-004 (phase-3 RCT, Fenaux et al., Blood 2011) — at 10 mg PO d1-21/28d: ~56% achieve RBC transfusion independence vs 5.9% placebo at 26 weeks; ~20-25% achieve cytogenetic CR (loss of del(5q) clone). Mechanism: cereblon-mediated selective degradation of CK1α encoded within the 5q33.1 commonly-deleted region — del(5q) cells haploinsufficient and uniquely sensitive. CRITICAL: TP53 co-mutation (~20% of del(5q) MDS) predicts lenalidomide resistance + higher AML transformation risk (~30-40% at 2 years vs ~10% TP53-WT) — TP53 NGS screening mandatory before initiating lenalidomide. Triggers RF-MDS-DEL-5Q-ISOLATED (existing).

eNRGy (phase I/II pan-tumor, n=204): zen: eNRGy (fase I/II pan-tumor, n=204): zenocutuzumab é um HER2 x HER3 biespecífico que bloqueia de forma única a dimerização HER3, impulsionada pelo NRG1. NSCLC (n=93) ORR 37,2%, mDOR 14,9 mo, mPFS 6,8 mo. Adenocarcinoma pancreático (n =36) ORN 42%. Atividade independente do parceiro de fusão. A aprovação da FDA 2024-12 cobre BOTH NSCCL e pancreática. Prevalência de fuzsão NRG1 ~0,2% pan-cancer; gap de teste é o ringlet prático — DNA-só NGS falha rotineiramente NRG 1 (grandes pontos de ruptura intrônicos), ensaios de fusión RNA necessários. Este arquivo é ancorado com CPNSC (~46% da população tratada); o mesmo regime aplica-se ao NRG1-fusion+ pancreático e outros tumores sólidos. Geralmente bem tolerados; reações de perfusão + diarreia + fadiga são EAs dominantes; raras diminuições da FEVE.
eNRGy trial (NCT02912949): Phase II, NRG: eNRGy trial (NCT02912949): Phase II, NRG1-fusion-positive solid tumors (pan-tumor basket). NSCLC cohort: ORR 33%, mDOR 7.4 mo. Pancreatic adenocarcinoma cohort: ORR 40%, mDOR 7.4 mo. FDA accelerated approval Dec 2024 — confirmatory study required. NRG1 fusion testing requires RNA-based NGS (DNA NGS misses many fusions). Trial-source SRC for eNRGy not yet ingested into KB — FLAG for follow-up.
eXalt3 (NCT02767804): Phase III, treatme: eXalt3 (NCT02767804): Phase III, treatment-naive ALK-positive advanced NSCLC. Ensartinib vs crizotinib. mPFS 25.8 vs 12.7 mo (HR 0.51). Intracranial response superior to crizotinib. FDA approval Dec 2024 — first-line ALK+ NSCLC. Comparative positioning: alectinib, brigatinib, lorlatinib remain preferred 1L per NCCN/ESMO based on cross-trial PFS and mature CNS data; ensartinib provides additional 2nd-gen option. Distinguishing AE = rash. Trial-source SRC for eXalt3 not yet ingested into KB — FLAG for follow-up.
eXalt3 (phase III, n=290): ensartinib vs: eXalt3 (phase III, n=290): ensartinib vs crizotinib in 1L ALK-TKI-naive ALK+ advanced NSCLC. mPFS 25.8 vs 12.7 mo (HR 0.51), CNS ORR 64 vs 21% in patients with baseline brain mets. Distinguishing AE profile: rash + pruritus dominate (67% all-grade rash; ~12% Grade ≥3) vs alectinib's myalgia/hepatic profile or brigatinib's early pulmonary events. Single daily dose convenient. Choice within ALK 1L: alectinib (ALEX) remains the cross-trial reference for OS + tolerability; brigatinib (ALTA-1L) preferred for high CNS burden; ensartinib is a viable alternative when access / tolerability dictate, but generally not preferred over alectinib/brigatinib/lorlatinib (CROWN) where available. Lorlatinib (CROWN) shows the deepest 1L PFS but with neurocognitive trade-offs.

This biomarker-treatment interaction analysis is the primary evidence for ESMO 2023 escalation recommendation. ESMO-ESGO-ESTRO 2023 guidelines: p53-abn molecular subtype → recommended for adjuvant chemoRT ± maintenance chemotherapy regardless of stage. NCCN Uterine Neoplasms 2025: p53-abn molecular subtype is Category 1 indication for adjuvant combination chemotherapy + external beam RT (chemoRT) in high-risk patients. Standard carboplatin AUC5 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m² q3w x4-6 cycles combined with or sequenced around EBRT. Additional support: PORTEC-4a trial (ongoing) evaluates adjuvant therapy de-escalation/escalation based on molecular subtype — early data further validate molecular triage including p53-abn as high-risk group requiring escalation. The actionability here is PREDICTIVE (not merely prognostic): p53-abn specifically predicts benefit from chemotherapy intensification BEYOND standard RT, guiding treatment selection in clinical practice.

~5-10% of BRAF-mutant tumors overall (NS: ~5-10% of BRAF-mutant tumors overall (NSCLC, melanoma, CRC) are non-V600; proportion higher in lung adeno where Class II / Class III combined approach the V600 cohort. Distinct from V600 in BOTH biology and therapy. Class II (G469A, K601E, L597) — RAF dimer formation drives signalling; monomer-selective BRAF inhibitors fail; MEK inhibitor (trametinib / binimetinib) monotherapy may show partial activity; pan-RAF dimer inhibitors (e.g., naporafenib / belvarafenib / exarafenib, lifirafenib) in trial. Class III (D594, G466, N581) — kinase-impaired; require upstream RTK activity; treat per RTK driver if present (e.g., EGFR or KRAS-G12C co-mutation), else MEK inhibition limited rationale. CRC Class II / III almost always co-occur with RAS or other MAPK alteration — distinct from V600E CRC (which is targetable per BEACON). Practice gap: PCR-only V600 hot-spot testing misses non-V600 entirely; full BRAF-region NGS required to detect.

No directly approved targeted agent — CDK4/6 inhibitors (palbociclib, ribociclib, abemaciclib) are biologically rational (synthetic-lethal hypothesis: loss of p16 → reliance on CDK4/6) but no large positive trial in solid tumors outside HR+ breast.
